# Script introduction

This is the second of six R Markdown notebooks. It turns the 2026 GBIF download of Lycaenidae occurrence records into cleaned records and geographic range measures for every species of the trait table of `s01_prepare_traits`.

Records are assigned to the species of the trait table (GBIF Backbone keys, duplicate keys merged into clusters) and then cleaned by explicit rules: metadata filters, coordinate tests, a native-region filter based on country checklists, documented introductions and species-concept errors, and a proportional geographic-outlier rule. Every rule is a flag on the record, and three datasets select flags: `main`, `inclusive` (the least restrictive) and the stringent `strict_plus` used in the paper. For each dataset, latitudinal extent, circular longitudinal extent and minimum-convex-polygon (MCP) area are measured, with their 80% rarefaction stability for `main` and `strict_plus`.

The raw inputs are the GBIF download (`gbif_occurrences/`), native-region layers (`native_region_layers/`: Pinkert et al. 2022 checklists, GADM countries, RESOLVE realms), curated rule tables (`occurrence_cleaning/`), the GBIF Backbone snapshot, taxonomy tables and the Hausharter et al. (2023) expert ranges (`expert_ranges/`); the species table, synonym database and 2024 name crosswalk come from `s01_prepare_traits`. The main outputs are the cleaned records (`records_final.rds`) and the range table (`range_metrics.csv`), used by the later notebooks, together with the record counts, outlier groups and expert-range checks reported in the paper. A full run takes about 1 h on a 16 GB laptop (range measurement about 25 min with four workers) and needs up to about 8 GB of memory and 6 GB of temporary disk space.

# Setup

## Packages

`terra` and `sf` handle the spatial data and `data.table` the record tables. Packages used for a few functions only (`CoordinateCleaner`, `countrycode`, `geosphere`, `jsonlite`, `parallel`, `rlang`, `zip`) are called with `::`.

```{r load_packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(resrepo)
library(terra)
library(data.table)
library(sf)
```

## Variables

The thresholds and seeds of the cleaning rules and range measures are fixed here, grouped by the section that uses them; they are saved with the range table as `parameters.csv`. The number of parallel workers for the range measurement does not affect the results.

```{r setup_variables}
# Thresholds and seeds of the cleaning rules and range measures, grouped by the section that
# uses them
parameters <- list(
  # --- Country and realm geometry ---
  # A listed country supports realms covering >= 5% of its land
  realm_min_country_share = 0.05,

  # --- Record metadata flags ---
  # Older records are flagged; records without a year are kept
  year_min = 1900,

  # Larger counts indicate aggregated or erroneous records
  individual_count_max = 1000,

  # Fossils and captive specimens are excluded by basis of record from main and strict_plus
  # (inclusive excludes only fossils)
  excluded_basis_of_record = c("FOSSIL_SPECIMEN", "LIVING_SPECIMEN"),

  # Establishment means that mark a record as non-native
  excluded_establishment_means = c("introduced", "invasive", "managed", "naturalised"),

  # Coordinate uncertainty limits (m) of main and strict_plus, and of inclusive
  uncertainty_max_main_m = 25000,
  uncertainty_max_inclusive_m = 100000,

  # A missing uncertainty is accepted with >= 2 decimals (about 1 km)
  na_uncertainty_min_decimals = 2,

  # --- Coordinate tests and the capital rule of the native-region filter ---
  # The CoordinateCleaner capital test uses a 10 km buffer (all datasets). Within that buffer,
  # records within 1 km of a capital are removed, and so are records within 10 km if the
  # uncertainty is missing or > 5 km or a coordinate has < 3 decimals.
  capital_buffer_inclusive_m = 10000,
  capital_buffer_strict_m = 1000,
  capital_imprecise_m = 5000,
  capital_min_decimals = 3,

  # --- Native-region filter ---
  # Equal Earth cells of the native-region and outlier rules (km)
  outlier_cell_km = 25,

  # Cells within 300 km of the listed area are consistent with it
  pinkert_reliability_buffer_km = 300,

  # Below this share of consistent cells the checklist is not used
  pinkert_reliability_min_coverage = 0.8,

  # main: remove cells > 300 km away in an unsupported realm, or > 1,000 km away in any realm
  pinkert_remove_other_realm_km = 300,
  pinkert_remove_any_realm_km = 1000,

  # strict_plus: remove all cells > 300 km away
  pinkert_remove_strict_km = 300,

  # Without a usable checklist, a realm with >= 10% of the cells or cells from >= 2 datasets is
  # native, and cells > 300 km from native-realm cells are removed
  fallback_realm_min_cell_share = 0.1,
  fallback_realm_min_datasets = 2,
  fallback_remove_km = 300,

  # --- Outlier rule ---
  # Coarser cells (50 km) for species occupying more than 4,000 of the 25-km cells
  outlier_cell_km_large = 50,
  outlier_large_cells = 4000,

  # main: the gap must exceed half the remaining diameter and 250 km
  outlier_f_main = 0.5,
  outlier_floor_main_km = 250,

  # strict_plus: the gap must exceed a quarter of the diameter and 200 km
  outlier_f_strict = 0.25,
  outlier_floor_strict_km = 200,

  # An outlier group holds at most 10% of the localities (or two)
  outlier_minority_share = 0.1,

  # main keeps a group recorded by >= 2 datasets, or by one dataset in >= 2 years and by >= 2
  # recorders, within 100 km of each other
  corroboration_min_datasets = 2,
  corroboration_single_dataset_years = 2,
  corroboration_single_dataset_recorders = 2,
  corroboration_radius_km = 100,

  # --- Range measurement and range table ---
  # Minimum unique localities for range measures
  min_unique_localities = 5,

  # Species below this number of localities are flagged as low-data
  low_data_localities = 10,

  # Coarse Equal Earth thinning (cells in km) for species spanning > 5 cells
  thin_cell_km = 50,

  # Minimum great-circle distance between thinned localities (km)
  thin_distance_km = 10,

  # Per-species seed = this + GBIF key
  thin_seed = 20240926,

  # Random 80% subsamples of the stability measure
  rarefaction_reps = 1000,

  # Per-species seed = this + GBIF key
  rarefaction_seed = 20240401
)

# Parallel workers of the range measurement (they do not affect the results)
n_workers <- 4
```

## Folders

Raw inputs are read from the versioned raw data and the trait tables from the folder of `s01_prepare_traits`; outputs are written to this notebook's folder in the versioned intermediate data. The input and output lists of the sections below give paths relative to these folders (`s01/` for the trait tables).

```{r setup_folders}
# Raw data and the trait tables of s01
dir_data_raw <- path_resrepo("data/raw")
dir_s01 <- path_resrepo("data/intermediate/s01_prepare_traits")

# Outputs of this notebook
dir_data_intermediate <- path_resrepo("data/intermediate/s02_prepare_ranges")
dir.create(dir_data_intermediate, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Functions

`write_table()` writes the output tables, `name_matching.R` matches checklist names to the GBIF Backbone snapshot, and `projections.R` and `range_metrics.R` hold the equal-area grids and range measures shared with the later notebooks.

```{r load_functions}
# Output tables
source(here::here("code", "R", "write_table.R"))

# Matching of checklist names to the GBIF Backbone snapshot
source(here::here("code", "R", "name_matching.R"))

# Equal-area grids and range measures shared with the later notebooks
source(here::here("code", "R", "projections.R"))
source(here::here("code", "R", "range_metrics.R"))
```

Tables are read with every column as character, so that GBIF keys and codes keep their exact text.

```{r define_readers}
# Read a CSV with all columns as character and empty strings or "NA" as missing
read_chr <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", na.strings = c("", "NA"),
           check.names = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
}
```

Each section below reads its inputs from disk and ends by removing its objects (in a hidden chunk), so only the objects defined in this setup carry over from one section to the next.

```{r keep_setup_objects}
# Objects of the setup, kept when each section clears its own objects
setup_objects <- c(ls(), "setup_objects")
```

# Frozen inputs

The records come from GBIF download 0009920-260928105237408 (GBIF.org, 4 October 2026, doi 10.15468/dl.58kd9b; licence CC BY-NC 4.0). It was requested on gbif.org for occurrence status PRESENT and taxon key C98 (Lycaenidae in Catalogue of Life XR), interpreted with the GBIF Backbone Taxonomy (checklist d7dddbf4-2cf0-4f39-9b2a-bb099caae36c) and exported as tab-separated SIMPLE_CSV with 10,797,420 records. The data bundle keeps the CSV, renamed `gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.csv`, in `gbif_occurrences/gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.zip`, beside metadata that record its size and md5 checksum. The chunk below, which is not run, shows how to rebuild the zip from GBIF; the GBIF import below checks the checksum.

```{r rebuild_gbif_download, eval = FALSE}
# --- Download the zip from GBIF ---
key <- "0009920-260928105237408"
tmp <- tempfile("gbif_")
dir.create(tmp)
download.file(paste0("https://api.gbif.org/v1/occurrence/download/request/", key, ".zip"),
              file.path(tmp, "download.zip"), mode = "wb")
zip::unzip(file.path(tmp, "download.zip"), exdir = tmp)

# --- Rename the CSV and zip it into the data bundle ---
# The download's only file is the CSV
file.rename(list.files(tmp, pattern = "[.]csv$", full.names = TRUE),
            file.path(tmp, "gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.csv"))
zip::zip(file.path(dir_data_raw, "gbif_occurrences", "gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.zip"),
         "gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.csv", root = tmp)
```

The native-region layers were downloaded on 4 October 2026: the country checklists of Pinkert et al. (2022; Map of Life, doi 10.48600/mol-1sr2-nh14, version 4), GADM 3.6 level-0 countries with ten small territories that the simplified 3.6 world layer omits taken from GADM 4.1 (GADM licence: academic and non-commercial use, no redistribution), and RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017 (Dinerstein et al. 2017; CC BY 4.0). The chunk below, which is not run, downloads them again.

```{r download_native_region_layers, eval = FALSE}
# Download one file into the native_region_layers folder; `...` is its path below that folder
get <- function(url, ...) {
  dest <- file.path(dir_data_raw, "native_region_layers", ...)
  dir.create(dirname(dest), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  download.file(url, dest, mode = "wb")
}

# --- Pinkert et al. (2022) country checklists ---
get("https://storage.googleapis.com/cdn.mol.org/dataset_downloads/butterflies_country_checklist_v4.csv",
    "pinkert_2022", "butterflies_country_checklist_v4.csv")

# --- GADM countries ---
# GADM 3.6 level-0 countries, and ten small territories from GADM 4.1
get("https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm3.6/gadm36_adm0_r1_pk.rds",
    "gadm", "gadm36_adm0_r1_pk.rds")
for (iso in c("CCK", "GIB", "MCO", "MDV", "MHL", "TKL", "TUV", "VAT", "XPI", "XSP")) {
  f <- paste0("gadm41_", iso, "_0_pk.rds")
  get(paste0("https://geodata.ucdavis.edu/gadm/gadm4.1/pck/", f), "gadm", "gadm41_small", f)
}

# --- RESOLVE Ecoregions 2017 ---
get("https://storage.googleapis.com/teow2016/Ecoregions2017.zip",
    "resolve_2017", "Ecoregions2017.zip")
```

Two tables freeze answers of live web services and are read as data: `gbif_backbone/pinkert_name_match_cache.csv` holds GBIF species-match responses (strict matching, 4 October 2026) for checklist names that the other matching tiers leave unresolved, and `occurrence_cleaning/doubtful_key_map.csv` maps 17 DOUBTFUL Backbone species keys to species of the universe when the epithet is identical or a gender variant and the GBIF record-country composition overlaps by at least 0.5 with exactly one species (built on 7 October 2026 from GBIF country facets). The rules for introduced populations (nine cited cases) and species-concept exclusions (four cases) are curated tables in `occurrence_cleaning/`.

# Checklist names

The country checklists of Pinkert et al. (2022) use the Lamas (2015) taxonomy. Their names are matched to the species of the trait table in tiers (Backbone snapshot, subspecies synonyms, verbatim alternatives, genus synonyms, reviewed name decisions, frozen GBIF matches); cross-genus epithet matches are never applied. The output lists the countries in which each species is recorded.

*Inputs:* native_region_layers/pinkert_2022/butterflies_country_checklist_v4.csv; gbif_backbone/ snapshot and pinkert_name_match_cache.csv; taxonomy/riodinid_genera.csv; trait_evidence/decisions/name_decisions.csv; s01/species_traits.csv  
*Output:* pinkert/pinkert_species_countries.csv (representative key x country)

```{r read_checklist_inputs}
# --- Checklist and Backbone snapshot ---
# The checklist must have the expected number of rows, with a name and a country on each
pk <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "native_region_layers", "pinkert_2022",
                         "butterflies_country_checklist_v4.csv"))
stopifnot(nrow(pk) == 87506L, !anyNA(pk$scientificname), !anyNA(pk$iso3))

# Accepted species, synonyms and doubtful names of the Backbone snapshot
acc <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "gbif_backbone", "accepted_species_20261002.csv"))
syn <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "gbif_backbone", "synonyms_20261002.csv"))
dbt <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "gbif_backbone", "doubtful_20261002.csv"))

# --- Trait table and name decisions ---
traits <- read_chr(file.path(dir_s01, "species_traits.csv"))
decisions <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "trait_evidence", "decisions",
                                "name_decisions.csv"))

# Representative key of each GBIF key
rep_of <- setNames(traits$representative_key, traits$gbif_key)

# Riodinid genera, which are skipped
riodinid <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "taxonomy", "riodinid_genera.csv"))$genus
```

## Lycaenidae candidates

The checklists have no family column. A name is a candidate if its genus is any genus-level name attached to Lycaenidae in the Backbone (accepted genera, synonym genera, genera of synonyms or doubtful names); genus homonyms in other families are caught by the family check of tier 5. Riodinid genera are skipped.

```{r find_lycaenid_candidates}
# --- Lycaenidae-linked genera ---
# Any genus-level name attached to Lycaenidae in the Backbone
lyc_genera <- unique(na.omit(c(
  acc$genus, syn$genus, dbt$genus,
  syn$canonicalName[syn$rank == "GENUS"], dbt$canonicalName[dbt$rank == "GENUS"]
)))

# --- Candidate checklist names ---
# Unique checklist names with their normalised name and genus
names_tab <- unique(pk[c("scientificname")])
nn <- normalise_name(names_tab$scientificname)
names_tab$normalised <- nn$normalised
names_tab$genus <- nn$genus

# Names in Lycaenidae-linked genera, except riodinid genera
cand <- names_tab[!is.na(names_tab$genus) & names_tab$genus %in% lyc_genera &
                    !names_tab$genus %in% riodinid, ]
cat("Pinkert names:", nrow(names_tab),
    "; in Lycaenidae-linked genera (excl. Riodinidae):", nrow(cand),
    "; riodinid-genus names skipped:",
    sum(names_tab$genus %in% intersect(lyc_genera, riodinid)), "\n")

# --- Verbatim alternatives ---
# Verbatim alternative names of each accepted checklist name
verb <- unique(pk[c("scientificname", "verbatimscientificname")])
alt_of <- lapply(split(verb$verbatimscientificname, verb$scientificname), function(v) {
  a <- unique(trimws(unlist(strsplit(v, ";"))))
  a[!is.na(a) & nzchar(a)]
})

# --- Backbone lookups ---
# Match types that count as a match to the snapshot
ok_types <- c("accepted_exact", "accepted_and_synonym", "synonym_resolved",
              "gender_variant_accepted", "gender_variant_synonym")

# Accepted key by canonical name, keeping only names that occur once
acc_key_by_name <- stats::setNames(acc$key, acc$canonicalName)
acc_key_by_name <- acc_key_by_name[!duplicated(names(acc_key_by_name)) &
  !names(acc_key_by_name) %in% names(acc_key_by_name)[duplicated(names(acc_key_by_name))]]
```

## Tiers 1-2: Backbone snapshot

Names are matched to the snapshot as in `s01_prepare_traits`; a synonym whose accepted taxon is a subspecies is assigned to the parent species of that subspecies.

```{r match_snapshot_tiers}
# Match names to the snapshot (tier 1) and assign subspecies synonyms to the parent species
# (tier 2). Returns the match table of match_gbif_names() with a `tier` column.
match_snapshot <- function(x) {
  m <- match_gbif_names(x, acc, syn, dbt)
  m$tier <- ifelse(m$match_type %in% ok_types, "1_snapshot", NA)

  # Tier 2: a synonym whose accepted taxon is a subspecies -> its parent species
  i <- which(m$match_type == "synonym_to_infraspecific")
  for (j in i) {
    s <- syn[syn$rank == "SPECIES" & syn$canonicalName == m$normalised[j], ]
    parents <- unique(vapply(strsplit(sub(" [(].*$", "", s$accepted), " "),
                             function(w) paste(w[1:2], collapse = " "), ""))
    keys <- unique(na.omit(acc_key_by_name[parents]))
    if (length(keys) == 1L) {
      m$accepted_key[j] <- keys
      m$accepted_name[j] <- names(acc_key_by_name)[match(keys, acc_key_by_name)]
      m$match_type[j] <- "synonym_of_subspecies_parent"
      m$note[j] <- paste("Backbone treats it as infraspecific:",
                         paste(unique(s$accepted), collapse = " | "))
      m$tier[j] <- "2_subspecies_parent"
    }
  }
  m
}

# --- Match the candidate names ---
res <- match_snapshot(cand$normalised)
res$pinkert_name <- cand$scientificname
res$matched_via <- ifelse(is.na(res$tier), NA, res$pinkert_name)
```

## Tier 3: verbatim alternatives

A name still unmatched is tried through the verbatim names that the checklist lists for it; all matched alternatives must point to one species.

```{r match_verbatim_alternatives}
# Names still unmatched
todo <- which(is.na(res$tier))
for (j in todo) {
  # Verbatim alternatives of the name, other than the name itself
  alts <- setdiff(alt_of[[res$pinkert_name[j]]], res$pinkert_name[j])
  if (!length(alts)) next

  # The alternatives that match the snapshot must all point to one species
  am <- match_snapshot(normalise_name(alts)$normalised)
  hit <- which(!is.na(am$tier))
  keys <- unique(am$accepted_key[hit])
  if (length(keys) == 1L) {
    h <- hit[1]
    res[j, c("match_type", "usage_key", "status", "accepted_key", "accepted_name", "note")] <-
      am[h, c("match_type", "usage_key", "status", "accepted_key", "accepted_name", "note")]
    res$tier[j] <- "3_verbatim_alternative"
    res$matched_via[j] <- alts[hit[1]]
  } else if (length(keys) > 1L) {
    res$note[j] <- paste("verbatim alternatives resolve to several species:",
                         paste(unique(am$accepted_name[hit]), collapse = " | "))
  }
}
```

## Tier 3b: same epithet under a Backbone genus synonym

If the checklist genus is a genus-rank synonym in the Backbone, a unique hit of the epithet (or a gender variant) in the accepted genus is the same taxon under the Backbone's generic placement.

```{r match_genus_synonyms}
# Genus synonyms of the Backbone with their accepted genus
gsyn <- syn[syn$rank == "GENUS" & !is.na(syn$accepted), c("canonicalName", "accepted")]
gsyn$accepted_genus <- sub(" .*$", "", gsyn$accepted)

# Names still unmatched
todo <- which(is.na(res$tier) & !is.na(res$normalised))
for (j in todo) {
  # Genus and epithet of the name; the genus must be a synonym of one accepted genus
  g <- sub(" .*$", "", res$normalised[j])
  e <- sub("^[^ ]+ ", "", res$normalised[j])
  targets <- unique(gsyn$accepted_genus[gsyn$canonicalName == g])
  if (length(targets) != 1L) next

  # The epithet (or a gender variant) must have a unique hit in the accepted genus
  cands <- paste(targets, epithet_variants(e))
  keys <- unique(na.omit(acc_key_by_name[cands]))
  if (length(keys) == 1L) {
    res$accepted_key[j] <- keys
    res$accepted_name[j] <- names(acc_key_by_name)[match(keys, acc_key_by_name)]
    res$match_type[j] <- "genus_synonym_transfer"
    res$note[j] <- paste0("Backbone: genus ", g, " is a synonym of ", targets)
    res$tier[j] <- "3b_genus_synonym"
  }
}
```

## Tier 4: reviewed name decisions of the trait table

The reviewed genus transfers, spelling variants and subspecies decisions of `s01_prepare_traits` are applied.

```{r apply_name_decisions}
# Reviewed decisions that give an accepted key
dec_ok <- decisions[decisions$decision %in% c("genus_transfer", "spelling_variant",
                                              "infraspecific_to_species") &
                      grepl("^[0-9]+$", decisions$accepted_key), ]

# Apply them to the names still unmatched
todo <- which(is.na(res$tier))
hit <- match(res$normalised[todo], dec_ok$normalised_name)
for (k in which(!is.na(hit))) {
  j <- todo[k]
  r <- dec_ok[hit[k], ]
  res$accepted_key[j] <- r$accepted_key
  res$accepted_name[j] <- acc$canonicalName[match(r$accepted_key, acc$key)]
  res$match_type[j] <- paste0("name_decision_", r$decision)
  res$note[j] <- r$reason
  res$tier[j] <- "4_name_decision"
}
```

## Tier 5: frozen GBIF species-match responses

Live answers of the GBIF species-match service can change, so the stored responses are read. Only exact matches at species or subspecies rank to species of the universe are accepted.

```{r match_frozen_gbif_responses}
# --- Stored responses ---
cache <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "gbif_backbone", "pinkert_name_match_cache.csv"))
todo <- which(is.na(res$tier) & !is.na(res$normalised))

# Every name still unmatched must have a stored response
missing <- setdiff(res$normalised[todo], cache$query)
if (length(missing)) stop(length(missing),
                          " checklist names have no stored GBIF match response, e.g. ",
                          missing[1], call. = FALSE)

# Stored response of each name, and the species keys of the universe
cm <- cache[match(res$normalised[todo], cache$query), ]
universe_keys <- traits$gbif_key[traits$universe_status == "gbif_accepted"]

# --- Accept exact matches ---
for (k in seq_along(todo)) {
  j <- todo[k]
  r <- cm[k, ]
  if (is.na(r$matchType) || r$matchType == "NONE") next

  # Names that GBIF places outside Lycaenidae
  if (!identical(r$family, "Lycaenidae")) {
    res$match_type[j] <- "not_lycaenidae"
    res$note[j] <- paste0("GBIF: ", r$canonicalName, " (", r$family, ", ", r$matchType, ")")
    next
  }

  # Exact matches at species or subspecies rank to a species of the universe are accepted;
  # other matches are only recorded in the note
  if (r$matchType == "EXACT" && r$rank %in% c("SPECIES", "SUBSPECIES") &&
      !is.na(r$speciesKey) && r$speciesKey %in% universe_keys) {
    res$accepted_key[j] <- r$speciesKey
    res$accepted_name[j] <- r$species
    res$usage_key[j] <- r$usageKey
    res$status[j] <- r$status
    res$match_type[j] <- paste0("gbif_api_", tolower(r$status), "_", tolower(r$rank))
    res$tier[j] <- "5_gbif_api"
  } else {
    res$note[j] <- paste0("GBIF API: ", r$canonicalName, " ", r$rank, " ", r$status,
                          " ", r$matchType, "; not auto-accepted")
  }
}
```

## Representative keys

Matched keys are mapped to the representative key of their duplicate cluster.

```{r map_representative_keys}
# Representative key of each matched name
res$representative_key <- unname(rep_of[res$accepted_key])

# A matched key outside the species universe is not a match
bad <- !is.na(res$tier) & is.na(res$representative_key)
if (any(bad)) {
  res$note[bad] <- paste("accepted key not in the species universe;", res$note[bad])
  res$tier[bad] <- NA
  res$match_type[bad] <- "key_outside_universe"
}
res$species <- traits$species[match(res$representative_key, traits$gbif_key)]

# Final status of each name: matched, not a Lycaenidae, or unmatched
res$status_final <- ifelse(!is.na(res$tier), "matched",
                           ifelse(res$match_type == "not_lycaenidae", "not_lycaenidae",
                                  "unmatched"))
```

## Species x country table

Each representative species receives the union of the countries of all checklist names matched to it.

```{r species_country_table}
# --- Countries of each representative species ---
# Matched names with their representative species
mt <- res[res$status_final == "matched",
          c("pinkert_name", "representative_key", "species", "tier")]

# One row per species and country: the union of the sources and checklist names
pc <- merge(pk[c("scientificname", "iso3", "source")], mt,
            by.x = "scientificname", by.y = "pinkert_name")
sc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pc, paste(pc$representative_key, pc$iso3)), function(z) {
  data.frame(representative_key = z$representative_key[1],
             species = z$species[1],
             iso3 = z$iso3[1],
             sources = paste(sort(unique(trimws(unlist(strsplit(z$source, ";"))))),
                             collapse = "; "),
             pinkert_names = paste(sort(unique(z$scientificname)), collapse = "; "),
             # TRUE when every source entry is specimen_rec_gbif
             gbif_specimen_only = all(trimws(z$source) == "specimen_rec_gbif"),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
sc <- sc[order(sc$species, sc$iso3), ]
write_table(sc, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "pinkert", "pinkert_species_countries.csv"))

# --- Summary ---
# Representative species of the universe, and those receiving several checklist names
reps <- traits$gbif_key[traits$universe_status == "gbif_accepted" &
                          traits$gbif_key == traits$representative_key &
                          !traits$genus %in% riodinid]
several <- names(which(table(mt$representative_key) > 1L))
print(rbind(
  data.frame(item = "pinkert_names_total", n = nrow(names_tab)),
  data.frame(item = "pinkert_names_in_lycaenidae_genera", n = nrow(cand)),
  data.frame(item = paste0("status_", names(table(res$status_final))),
             n = as.integer(table(res$status_final))),
  data.frame(item = paste0("tier_", names(table(res$tier))),
             n = as.integer(table(res$tier))),
  data.frame(item = "universe_representative_species", n = length(reps)),
  data.frame(item = "universe_species_with_pinkert_countries",
             n = sum(reps %in% sc$representative_key)),
  data.frame(item = "universe_species_receiving_several_pinkert_names",
             n = sum(reps %in% several)),
  data.frame(item = "species_country_rows", n = nrow(sc))
), row.names = FALSE)
```

# Country and realm geometry

GADM countries and RESOLVE biogeographic realms (Dinerstein et al. 2017) are rasterised onto a 0.05-degree grid. A country supports the realms covering at least 5% of its land, and the supported country-realm parts form each species' "listed area", so that remote territories (e.g. Hawaii within the USA) do not validate records. The country raster also serves as the land mask of the sea test.

*Inputs:* native_region_layers/gadm/{gadm36_adm0_r1_pk.rds, gadm41_small/*.rds}; native_region_layers/resolve_2017/Ecoregions2017.zip; native_region_layers/pinkert_2022/butterflies_country_checklist_v4.csv; pinkert/pinkert_species_countries.csv  
*Outputs:* geometry/realm_0p05.tif, geometry/country_0p05.tif, geometry/realm_codes.csv, geometry/country_realm_support.csv, geometry/country_realm_parts.gpkg, geometry/pinkert_species_realms.csv

```{r geometry_folder}
# terra writes only to existing folders
out_dir <- file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Countries

GADM 3.6 countries are completed with ten small territories from GADM 4.1, and every checklist country must have a geometry.

```{r read_countries}
# --- GADM countries ---
# GADM 3.6 countries, completed with ten small territories from GADM 4.1
world <- unwrap(readRDS(file.path(dir_data_raw, "native_region_layers", "gadm",
                                  "gadm36_adm0_r1_pk.rds")))
world <- world[, "GID_0"]
small_files <- list.files(file.path(dir_data_raw, "native_region_layers", "gadm", "gadm41_small"),
                          pattern = "[.]rds$", full.names = TRUE)
small <- do.call(rbind, lapply(small_files, function(f) unwrap(readRDS(f))[, "GID_0"]))
small_codes <- small$GID_0
countries <- rbind(world[!world$GID_0 %in% small_codes, ], small)

# Numeric id of each country
country_codes <- data.frame(country_id = seq_len(nrow(countries)), iso3 = countries$GID_0)
countries$country_id <- country_codes$country_id

# --- Checklist countries ---
# Every checklist country must have a geometry
pk <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "native_region_layers", "pinkert_2022",
                         "butterflies_country_checklist_v4.csv"))
missing <- setdiff(unique(pk$iso3), country_codes$iso3)
if (length(missing)) stop("Pinkert countries without geometry: ",
                          paste(missing, collapse = " "))
```

## Realms

The RESOLVE ecoregions give the realms; their unnamed realm of rock and ice is labelled.

```{r read_realms}
# --- RESOLVE ecoregions ---
# Read from inside the zip file; the unnamed realm of rock and ice is labelled
eco <- vect(paste0("/vsizip/",
                   file.path(dir_data_raw, "native_region_layers", "resolve_2017",
                             "Ecoregions2017.zip"),
                   "/Ecoregions2017.shp"))
eco$REALM[eco$REALM == "N/A"] <- "Rock and ice"

# --- Realm codes ---
# Numeric id of each realm (in alphabetical order)
realm_codes <- data.frame(realm_id = seq_along(sort(unique(eco$REALM))),
                          realm = sort(unique(eco$REALM)))
eco$realm_id <- realm_codes$realm_id[match(eco$REALM, realm_codes$realm)]
```

## Rasterise

Countries and realms are rasterised onto a 0.05-degree grid, where small territories win the cells they touch. Country cells without a realm take the modal realm of their neighbours, and remote atolls missing from RESOLVE the realm of the nearest ecoregion.

```{r rasterise_geometry}
# --- Grid and helper ---
# Global grid of 0.05 degrees
grid <- rast(ext(-180, 180, -90, 90), resolution = 0.05, crs = "EPSG:4326")

# Fill the empty cells of the raster r from a rasterisation of the polygons v in which every
# cell touched by a polygon counts. Returns the completed raster; cells of r keep their value.
fill_touches <- function(r, v, field) {
  t <- rasterize(v, grid, field = field, touches = TRUE)
  cover(r, t)
}

# --- Realm and country rasters ---
realm_r <- rasterize(eco, grid, field = "realm_id")
realm_r <- fill_touches(realm_r, eco, "realm_id")

# Countries other than the small territories
big <- countries[!countries$GID_0 %in% small_codes, ]
country_r <- rasterize(big, grid, field = "country_id")
country_r <- fill_touches(country_r, big, "country_id")

# Small territories win the cells they touch
small_v <- countries[countries$GID_0 %in% small_codes, ]
small_r <- rasterize(small_v, grid, field = "country_id", touches = TRUE)
country_r <- cover(small_r, country_r)

# Warn about countries left without any cell
present <- unique(values(country_r, na.rm = TRUE))
lost <- setdiff(country_codes$country_id, present)
if (length(lost)) warning("countries without any cell: ",
                          paste(country_codes$iso3[lost], collapse = " "))

# --- Realm for country cells without one ---
# Modal value of the neighbouring cells, iterated
need <- !is.na(country_r) & is.na(realm_r)
cat("country cells without realm before filling:",
    global(need, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], "\n")
for (i in 1:10) {
  f <- focal(realm_r, w = 3, fun = "modal", na.policy = "only", na.rm = TRUE)
  realm_r <- ifel(is.na(realm_r) & !is.na(country_r), f, realm_r)
}
need <- !is.na(country_r) & is.na(realm_r)
cat("country cells without realm after modal filling:",
    global(need, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[[1]], "\n")

# Remaining land cells (remote atolls missing from RESOLVE, e.g. Tokelau, Nauru) take the
# realm of the nearest ecoregion. Antarctica and the Caspian Sea (GADM `XCA`) stay without a
# realm.
skip <- country_codes$country_id[country_codes$iso3 %in% c("ATA", "XCA")]
cells <- which(values(need)[, 1] == 1 & !values(country_r)[, 1] %in% skip)
if (length(cells)) {
  pts <- vect(xyFromCell(grid, cells), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  eco_simple <- simplifyGeom(eco, tolerance = 0.05)
  nn <- nearest(pts, eco_simple)
  realm_r[cells] <- eco_simple$realm_id[nn$to_id]
  cat("cells assigned to the nearest ecoregion's realm:", length(cells),
      "; max distance (km):", round(max(nn$distance) / 1000), "\n")
}

# --- Write the rasters and realm codes ---
names(realm_r) <- "realm_id"
names(country_r) <- "country_id"
writeRaster(realm_r, file.path(out_dir, "realm_0p05.tif"),
            overwrite = TRUE, datatype = "INT1U")
writeRaster(country_r, file.path(out_dir, "country_0p05.tif"),
            overwrite = TRUE, datatype = "INT2U")
write_table(realm_codes, file.path(out_dir, "realm_codes.csv"))
```

## Country x realm areas and support

A country supports the realms covering at least 5% of its land, and always its largest realm, except rock and ice and Antarctica.

```{r country_realm_support}
# --- Area of each country-realm part ---
# The part code is country_id * 100 + realm_id (realm_id < 100)
area <- cellSize(grid, unit = "km")
part_r <- country_r * 100 + realm_r
names(part_r) <- "part"
z <- zonal(area, part_r, fun = "sum", na.rm = TRUE)
names(z) <- c("part", "area_km2")
z$country_id <- z$part %/% 100
z$realm_id <- z$part %% 100
z$iso3 <- country_codes$iso3[match(z$country_id, country_codes$country_id)]
z$realm <- realm_codes$realm[match(z$realm_id, realm_codes$realm_id)]

# --- Share of the country and realm support ---
# Share of each part in the land of its country, and the largest realm of each country
z$country_area_km2 <- ave(z$area_km2, z$iso3, FUN = sum)
z$share <- z$area_km2 / z$country_area_km2
z$largest <- ave(z$share, z$iso3, FUN = max) == z$share

# A realm is supported when it covers enough of the country or is the largest, except rock and
# ice and Antarctica
z$supported <- (z$share >= parameters$realm_min_country_share | z$largest) &
  !z$realm %in% c("Rock and ice", "Antarctica")
z <- z[order(z$iso3, -z$share), c("iso3", "realm", "part", "area_km2", "country_area_km2",
                                  "share", "largest", "supported")]
write_table(z, file.path(out_dir, "country_realm_support.csv"))

# --- Checks ---
# Countries with more than one supported realm
cat("\ncountries with >1 supported realm:\n")
multi <- z[z$supported & ave(z$supported, z$iso3, FUN = sum) > 1,
           c("iso3", "realm", "share")]
print(multi, row.names = FALSE)

# A selection of countries
cat("\nselected checks:\n")
print(z[z$iso3 %in% c("USA", "MEX", "CHN", "IDN", "YEM", "IND",
                      "PNG", "AUS", "FRA", "ESP", "EGY"),
        c("iso3", "realm", "share", "supported")],
      row.names = FALSE)
```

## Supported parts as polygons

The supported country-realm parts are saved as polygons, from which the native-region filter measures distances.

```{r supported_parts}
# Polygons of the supported country-realm parts, dissolved by part code
supported_parts <- z$part[z$supported]
sp_r <- classify(part_r, cbind(supported_parts, supported_parts), others = NA)
parts <- as.polygons(sp_r, dissolve = TRUE)

# Country, realm and share of country of each part
parts$iso3 <- z$iso3[match(parts$part, z$part)]
parts$realm <- z$realm[match(parts$part, z$part)]
parts$share <- z$share[match(parts$part, z$part)]
writeVector(parts, file.path(out_dir, "country_realm_parts.gpkg"), overwrite = TRUE)
cat("\nsupported country-realm parts:", nrow(parts), "\n")
```

## Supported realms per species

The supported realms of each species' checklist countries become a column of the range table.

```{r species_realms}
# Supported realms of the countries of each species
sc <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "pinkert", "pinkert_species_countries.csv"))
sup <- z[z$supported, c("iso3", "realm")]
m <- merge(sc[c("representative_key", "species", "iso3")], sup, by = "iso3")

# One row per species, with its realms joined by "; " and their number
sr <- aggregate(realm ~ representative_key + species, m,
                function(v) paste(sort(unique(v)), collapse = "; "))
names(sr)[3] <- "supported_realms"
sr$n_realms <- lengths(strsplit(sr$supported_realms, "; "))
write_table(sr, file.path(out_dir, "pinkert_species_realms.csv"))
cat("species with Pinkert realms:", nrow(sr), "\n")
print(table(sr$n_realms))
```

# GBIF import

The download is checked (size, md5, integer Backbone keys) and read with the columns needed later; records without coordinates are dropped.

*Inputs:* gbif_occurrences/gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.zip and .json  
*Output:* records_imported.rds

```{r import_gbif_records}
# --- Download metadata ---
meta <- jsonlite::fromJSON(file.path(dir_data_raw, "gbif_occurrences",
                                     "gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.json"))

# --- Extract and check the CSV ---
# R's internal unzip truncates files of 4 GB or more, so the zip package (Zip64 support)
# extracts the CSV into a temporary folder; the extracted copy is checked against the metadata
# and deleted after reading.
exdir <- tempfile("gbif_download_")
dir.create(exdir)
zip::unzip(file.path(dir_data_raw, "gbif_occurrences", "gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.zip"),
           files = "gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.csv", exdir = exdir)
csv <- file.path(exdir, "gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.csv")
if (!isTRUE(file.size(csv) == meta$size_bytes) || unname(tools::md5sum(csv)) != meta$md5)
  stop("The extracted CSV differs in size or md5 from gbif_download_lycaenidae_2026.json.",
       call. = FALSE)

# Read the selected columns of the CSV; the taxon keys are kept as text
reader <- function(select, nrows = Inf) {
  fread(file = csv, select = select, nrows = nrows, quote = "", showProgress = FALSE,
        colClasses = list(character = c("taxonKey", "speciesKey")))
}

# The keys must be integer GBIF Backbone keys, i.e. the download must be interpreted with
# the Backbone
head_rows <- reader(c("taxonKey", "speciesKey"), nrows = 1e5)
non_integer <- mean(!grepl("^[0-9]+$", head_rows$taxonKey[nzchar(head_rows$taxonKey)]))
if (non_integer > 0) stop(sprintf(
  "taxonKey is not an integer GBIF Backbone key in %.1f%% of the first rows (e.g. '%s'). ",
  100 * non_integer, head_rows$taxonKey[!grepl("^[0-9]+$", head_rows$taxonKey)][1]),
  "The download must be interpreted with the GBIF Backbone taxonomy.", call. = FALSE)

# --- Read the records ---
cols <- c("gbifID", "datasetKey", "species", "taxonRank", "scientificName",
          "verbatimScientificName", "taxonKey", "speciesKey", "decimalLatitude",
          "decimalLongitude", "coordinateUncertaintyInMeters", "coordinatePrecision",
          "countryCode", "occurrenceStatus", "individualCount", "basisOfRecord", "year",
          "establishmentMeans", "issue", "recordedBy", "institutionCode")
x <- reader(cols)
unlink(exdir, recursive = TRUE)

# Records without coordinates are dropped; the counts must match the metadata
audit <- data.frame(stage = "download_rows", records = nrow(x))
x <- x[!is.na(decimalLatitude) & !is.na(decimalLongitude)]
audit <- rbind(audit, data.frame(stage = "with_coordinates", records = nrow(x)))
stopifnot(audit$records == c(meta$rows, meta$rows_with_coordinates))

# --- GBIF issue flags ---
# Keep only the GBIF issue flags used as filters (the full string is large)
used_issues <- c("ZERO_COORDINATE", "COORDINATE_INVALID", "COORDINATE_OUT_OF_RANGE",
                 "COUNTRY_COORDINATE_MISMATCH", "PRESUMED_SWAPPED_COORDINATE",
                 "PRESUMED_NEGATED_LATITUDE", "PRESUMED_NEGATED_LONGITUDE",
                 "COORDINATE_REPROJECTION_FAILED", "TAXON_MATCH_FUZZY",
                 "TAXON_MATCH_HIGHERRANK", "COORDINATE_ROUNDED")
for (u in used_issues) set(x, j = paste0("issue_", tolower(u)),
                           value = grepl(u, x$issue, fixed = TRUE))
x[, issue := NULL]

# --- Save ---
saveRDS(x, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_imported.rds"), compress = "gzip")
print(audit)
cat("species (Backbone speciesKey):", uniqueN(x$speciesKey[nzchar(x$speciesKey)]), "\n")
```

```{r clear_import_gbif_records, include=FALSE}
invisible(gc())
```

# Taxonomic assignment

GBIF's species key is mapped to the representative key of its cluster in the trait table, so subspecies records join their species. Records on DOUBTFUL keys follow the frozen key map, and records that GBIF resolved only above species rank are assigned when their verbatim name exactly matches an accepted species or a reviewed synonym; no fuzzy matching is used.

*Inputs:* records_imported.rds; s01/{species_traits,synonym_database}.csv; occurrence_cleaning/doubtful_key_map.csv; taxonomy/riodinid_genera.csv  
*Output:* records_taxonomy.rds (adds rep_key, pool_key, rep_species, flag_taxon_*)

```{r assign_taxonomy}
# --- Records and species lookups ---
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_imported.rds"))
traits <- read_chr(file.path(dir_s01, "species_traits.csv"))
acc <- traits[traits$universe_status == "gbif_accepted", ]
rep_of <- setNames(acc$representative_key, acc$gbif_key)
sp_of <- setNames(acc$species, acc$gbif_key)

# --- Taxon flags and representative key ---
# Flags for records above species rank and for riodinid genera
x[, flag_taxon_rank := !taxonRank %in% c("SPECIES", "SUBSPECIES", "VARIETY", "FORM")]
x[, genus_name := sub(" .*$", "", species)]
riodinid <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "taxonomy", "riodinid_genera.csv"))$genus
x[, flag_taxon_riodinid := genus_name %in% riodinid]

# Representative key of the cluster of each GBIF species key
x[, rep_key := unname(rep_of[speciesKey])]

# --- DOUBTFUL Backbone keys ---
# Map rows whose target is no longer a representative (clusters changed after the map was
# built) are ignored.
dk <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "occurrence_cleaning", "doubtful_key_map.csv"))
dk <- dk[!is.na(dk$rep_key), ]
stale <- !dk$rep_key %in% acc$representative_key
if (any(stale)) {
  message(sum(stale), " DOUBTFUL-map rows point to keys that are no longer ",
          "representatives: ignored")
  dk <- dk[!stale, ]
}
hit <- is.na(x$rep_key) & x$speciesKey %in% dk$speciesKey
x[hit, rep_key := dk$rep_key[match(speciesKey, dk$speciesKey)]]
cat("records mapped from DOUBTFUL keys:", sum(hit), "\n")

# --- Verbatim-name recovery ---
# Records still without a key (except riodinids) are matched by their verbatim name,
# e.g. 'Chrysoritis zeuxo', absent from the Backbone and resolved to its genus. Accepted names
# take precedence over synonyms; recovered records keep GBIF's interpretation in taxonRank.
syn <- read_chr(file.path(dir_s01, "synonym_database.csv"))
syn <- syn[syn$gbif_accepted_key %in% acc$gbif_key &
             syn$resolution_confidence %in% c("high", "high_manual",
                                              "medium_orthographic_variant",
                                              "medium_reviewed_transfer"), ]

# Representative key by accepted name and by reviewed synonym name
name_rep <- c(setNames(acc$representative_key, acc$canonical),
              setNames(unname(rep_of[syn$gbif_accepted_key]),
                       gsub("_", " ", syn$normalised_name)))
name_rep <- name_rep[!duplicated(names(name_rep))]

# Genus and epithet of the verbatim name of each unassigned, non-riodinid record (NA when the
# name has another form)
cand <- is.na(x$rep_key) & !x$flag_taxon_riodinid
vb <- sub("^([A-Z][a-z]+) +[(]?[A-Z]?[a-z]*[)]? *([a-z][a-z-]+).*$", "\\1 \\2",
          trimws(x$verbatimScientificName[cand]))
vb[!grepl("^[A-Z][a-z]+ [a-z][a-z-]+$", vb)] <- NA
rec_key <- unname(name_rep[vb])

# Assign the recovered records
x[, taxon_recovered_verbatim := FALSE]
ii <- which(cand)[!is.na(rec_key)]
x[ii, `:=`(rep_key = rec_key[!is.na(rec_key)], flag_taxon_rank = FALSE,
           taxon_recovered_verbatim = TRUE)]
cat("records recovered from verbatim names:", length(ii),
    "; species:", uniqueN(x$rep_key[ii]), "\n")

# --- Records outside the species universe ---
x[, flag_taxon_outside_universe := !flag_taxon_rank & !flag_taxon_riodinid &
      is.na(rep_key)]

# Species name and pool key of each record (each species starts as its own pool)
x[, rep_species := unname(sp_of[rep_key])]
x[, genus_name := NULL]
x[, pool_key := rep_key]

# Species keys outside the universe, by number of records
um <- x[flag_taxon_outside_universe == TRUE, .(records = .N),
        by = .(speciesKey, species)][order(-records)]

# --- Summary and save ---
print(data.frame(
  stage = c("records_with_coordinates", "above_species_rank", "riodinidae",
            "species_key_outside_universe", "assigned_to_universe_species",
            "species_assigned", "recovered_from_verbatim_name"),
  n = c(nrow(x), sum(x$flag_taxon_rank), sum(x$flag_taxon_riodinid),
        sum(x$flag_taxon_outside_universe), sum(!is.na(x$rep_key)),
        uniqueN(x$rep_key, na.rm = TRUE), sum(x$taxon_recovered_verbatim))))
cat("largest unassigned keys:\n")
print(head(um, 15))
saveRDS(x, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_taxonomy.rds"), compress = "gzip")
```

# Record metadata flags

Each record-level rule becomes a flag: absence records, records before 1900, counts above 1,000 individuals, fossil and living specimens, records stated to be non-native, coordinate uncertainty above 25 km (main) or 100 km (inclusive), missing uncertainty with fewer than two decimals (main), and GBIF coordinate issues. GBIF taxon-match issues are recorded but not used, because at species rank they mostly mark correctly resolved subspecies names and spelling variants.

*Input:* records_taxonomy.rds  
*Output:* records_meta.rds

```{r flag_record_metadata}
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_taxonomy.rds"))

# --- Number of decimals ---
# Number of decimals as written. GBIF stores coordinates as numbers, so the shortest
# representation (up to 6 decimals) is used.
decimals <- function(v) {
  s <- sub("0+$", "", sprintf("%.6f", abs(v)))
  nchar(sub("^[0-9]*[.]?", "", s))
}

# --- Record metadata flags ---
# Absence, year, individual count, basis of record and establishment means
x[, flag_absent := !is.na(occurrenceStatus) & toupper(occurrenceStatus) == "ABSENT"]
x[, flag_year := !is.na(year) & year < parameters$year_min]
x[, flag_count := !is.na(individualCount) &
      (individualCount <= 0 | individualCount > parameters$individual_count_max)]
x[, flag_basis := basisOfRecord %in% parameters$excluded_basis_of_record]
x[, flag_establishment := tolower(establishmentMeans) %in%
      parameters$excluded_establishment_means]

# Coordinate uncertainty: the limit of inclusive, and the limit of main, where a missing
# uncertainty needs at least the minimum number of decimals
x[, flag_uncertainty_inclusive := !is.na(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters) &
      coordinateUncertaintyInMeters > parameters$uncertainty_max_inclusive_m]
x[, min_decimals := pmin(decimals(decimalLatitude), decimals(decimalLongitude))]
x[, flag_uncertainty_main :=
      (!is.na(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters) &
         coordinateUncertaintyInMeters > parameters$uncertainty_max_main_m) |
      (is.na(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters) &
         min_decimals < parameters$na_uncertainty_min_decimals)]

# --- GBIF issue flags ---
# Coordinate issues; the taxon-match issues are recorded but not used as a filter
x[, flag_gbif_coordinate_issue := issue_zero_coordinate | issue_coordinate_invalid |
      issue_coordinate_out_of_range | issue_country_coordinate_mismatch |
      issue_presumed_swapped_coordinate | issue_presumed_negated_latitude |
      issue_presumed_negated_longitude | issue_coordinate_reprojection_failed]
x[, flag_gbif_taxon_issue := issue_taxon_match_fuzzy | issue_taxon_match_higherrank]

# --- Summary and save ---
flags <- grep("^flag_", names(x), value = TRUE)
print(data.frame(flag = flags,
                 records = vapply(flags, function(f) sum(x[[f]]), 0),
                 share = vapply(flags, function(f) mean(x[[f]]), 0)),
      row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(x, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_meta.rds"), compress = "gzip")
```

```{r clear_flag_record_metadata, include=FALSE}
invisible(gc())
```

# Coordinate tests

CoordinateCleaner (Zizka et al. 2019) flags capitals, country and province centroids, biodiversity institutions, the GBIF headquarters, zero and equal coordinates; records with no land within about 10 km are flagged as at sea. The tests run once per unique coordinate.

*Inputs:* records_meta.rds; geometry/country_0p05.tif  
*Output:* records_coord.rds

```{r test_coordinates}
# --- Unique coordinates ---
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_meta.rds"))
u <- unique(x[, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)])
cat("records:", nrow(x), "; unique coordinates:", nrow(u), "\n")
u <- as.data.frame(u)

# --- CoordinateCleaner tests ---
# Run the CoordinateCleaner test f on the unique coordinates in blocks of 250,000 rows.
# Returns a logical vector, TRUE for the flagged coordinates; `...` are further arguments
# of f.
run <- function(f, ...) {
  out <- logical(nrow(u))
  chunk <- 250000L
  for (s in seq.int(1L, nrow(u), by = chunk)) {
    i <- s:min(s + chunk - 1L, nrow(u))
    out[i] <- !f(u[i, ], lon = "decimalLongitude", lat = "decimalLatitude",
                 value = "flagged", verbose = FALSE, ...)
  }
  out
}

# Capitals, country and province centroids, biodiversity institutions, the GBIF headquarters,
# zero and equal coordinates
u$flag_cc_capital <- run(CoordinateCleaner::cc_cap,
                         buffer = parameters$capital_buffer_inclusive_m)
u$flag_cc_centroid <- run(CoordinateCleaner::cc_cen, buffer = 1000, test = "both")
u$flag_cc_institution <- run(CoordinateCleaner::cc_inst, buffer = 100)
u$flag_cc_gbif_hq <- run(CoordinateCleaner::cc_gbif, buffer = 1000)
u$flag_cc_zero <- run(CoordinateCleaner::cc_zero, buffer = 0.5)
u$flag_cc_equal <- run(CoordinateCleaner::cc_equ, test = "absolute")

# --- At sea ---
# At sea: no land within two 0.05-degree cells (about 10 km). Coordinates with no value in the
# land raster are also flagged.
land <- rast(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry", "country_0p05.tif"))
land <- !is.na(land)
near_land <- focal(land, w = 5, fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE)
u$flag_sea <- extract(near_land,
                      as.matrix(u[c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude")]))[, 1] != 1
u$flag_sea[is.na(u$flag_sea)] <- TRUE

# --- Join to the records and save ---
x <- merge(x, as.data.table(u), by = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"), sort = FALSE)
flags <- grep("^flag_cc_|^flag_sea$", names(x), value = TRUE)
print(data.frame(flag = flags,
                 unique_coordinates = vapply(flags, function(f) sum(u[[f]]), 0),
                 records = vapply(flags, function(f) sum(x[[f]]), 0)),
      row.names = FALSE)
saveRDS(x, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_coord.rds"), compress = "gzip")
```

```{r clear_test_coordinates, include=FALSE}
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), setup_objects))
invisible(gc())
```

# Native-region filter

The base filters define the main and inclusive record sets; near capitals only records within 1 km, or within 10 km when imprecise, are removed. Records are grouped into 25-km Equal Earth cells. Where a species' records broadly agree with its checklist (at least 80% of cells within 300 km of the listed area), main removes cells more than 300 km from the listed area in an unsupported realm or more than 1,000 km away anywhere, and strict_plus removes all cells more than 300 km away. Otherwise, realms holding at least 10% of the species' cells or cells from at least two datasets are treated as native, cells in other realms more than 300 km from them are removed, and cells on another continent (more than 1,000 km from the listed area in a realm no listed country supports) are removed unless they are the majority.

*Inputs:* records_coord.rds; geometry/*; pinkert/pinkert_species_countries.csv  
*Outputs:* records_base.rds (slim record table with base flags and cell ids), native/species_native_summary.csv

```{r apply_base_filters}
# --- Capital rule ---
# Coordinates flagged by the capital test that lie within the strict capital buffer
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_coord.rds"))
cap_u <- unique(x[flag_cc_capital == TRUE, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)])
cap_u[, within_1km := !CoordinateCleaner::cc_cap(as.data.frame(cap_u),
                                                  lon = "decimalLongitude",
                                                  lat = "decimalLatitude",
                                                  buffer = parameters$capital_buffer_strict_m,
                                                  value = "flagged", verbose = FALSE)]
x <- merge(x, cap_u, by = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"),
           all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
x[is.na(within_1km), within_1km := FALSE]

# Imprecise records: uncertainty missing or above the limit, or too few decimals
x[, imprecise := (is.na(coordinateUncertaintyInMeters) |
                    coordinateUncertaintyInMeters > parameters$capital_imprecise_m) |
      min_decimals < parameters$capital_min_decimals]

# Main rule: a flagged record is removed if it is within the strict buffer or imprecise
x[, flag_cc_capital_main := flag_cc_capital & (within_1km | imprecise)]
cat("capital flag: 10 km rule", sum(x$flag_cc_capital),
    "records; main rule", sum(x$flag_cc_capital_main), "\n")

# --- Base filters ---
# Any coordinate test, with the main capital rule
cc_any_main <- x$flag_cc_capital_main | x$flag_cc_centroid | x$flag_cc_institution |
  x$flag_cc_gbif_hq | x$flag_cc_zero | x$flag_cc_equal

# Records of a species of the universe
taxon_ok <- !x$flag_taxon_rank & !x$flag_taxon_riodinid & !x$flag_taxon_outside_universe

# Base set of main: taxon, metadata, coordinate and sea filters. GBIF taxon-match issues are
# diagnostic only.
x[, base_main := taxon_ok & !flag_absent & !flag_year & !flag_count & !flag_basis &
      !flag_establishment & !flag_uncertainty_main & !flag_gbif_coordinate_issue &
      !cc_any_main & !flag_sea]

# Base set of the inclusive dataset (the least restrictive): only fossils are excluded by basis of
# record
x[, base_inclusive := taxon_ok & !flag_absent & !flag_year & !flag_count &
      !(basisOfRecord %in% "FOSSIL_SPECIMEN") & !flag_uncertainty_inclusive & !cc_any_main &
      !issue_country_coordinate_mismatch]
cat("records:", nrow(x), "; base_main:", sum(x$base_main),
    "; base_inclusive:", sum(x$base_inclusive), "\n")
```

## 25-km Equal Earth cells

Records are assigned to 25-km Equal Earth cells, realms and countries, and only the columns needed later are kept.

```{r assign_cells}
# --- 25-km cells ---
# 25-km Equal Earth cell of each record, projected in chunks of one million records (avoids
# running out of memory)
grid25 <- global_thinning_grid(parameters$outlier_cell_km)
ee <- crs(grid25)
cell25 <- integer(nrow(x))
for (s0 in seq(1L, nrow(x), by = 1000000L)) {
  i <- s0:min(s0 + 999999L, nrow(x))
  pts <- vect(as.matrix(x[i, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  cell25[i] <- cellFromXY(grid25, crds(project(pts, ee)))
}
x[, cell25 := cell25]
rm(pts, cell25)
invisible(gc())

# --- Realm and country ---
realm_r <- rast(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry", "realm_0p05.tif"))
realm_codes <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry", "realm_codes.csv"))
x[, realm_id := extract(realm_r,
                        as.matrix(x[, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]))[, 1]]
x[, realm := realm_codes$realm[match(realm_id, as.integer(realm_codes$realm_id))]]
x[, iso3 := countrycode::countrycode(countryCode, "iso2c", "iso3c", warn = FALSE)]

# Kosovo (country code XK) takes GADM's code XKO
x[countryCode == "XK", iso3 := "XKO"]

# --- Slim record table ---
# Only the columns needed later, with the base flags and cell ids
slim <- x[, .(gbifID, pool_key, rep_key, rep_species, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude,
              datasetKey, year, recordedBy, basisOfRecord, iso3, realm, cell25,
              base_main, base_inclusive)]
rm(x)
invisible(gc())
```

## Cell table for base_main

The filter works on the occupied cells of each species, each represented by its first record.

```{r occupied_cells}
# Occupied 25-km cells of each unit among the base_main records, each represented by the
# coordinates and realm of its first record
m <- slim[base_main == TRUE]
cells <- m[, .(lon = decimalLongitude[1], lat = decimalLatitude[1], n_records = .N,
               n_datasets = uniqueN(datasetKey),
               realm = realm[1]),
           by = .(pool_key, cell25)]
cat("species units:", uniqueN(cells$pool_key), "; occupied 25-km cells:", nrow(cells), "\n")
```

## Listed area per unit

Each cell's distance to the species' listed area decides whether the checklist is reliable for the species and which cells are removed; without a reliable checklist the realms supported by the records decide.

```{r native_region_rule}
# --- Geometry and checklists ---
# Supported country-realm parts (simplified), checklist countries and supported realms
parts <- vect(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry", "country_realm_parts.gpkg"))
parts <- simplifyGeom(parts, tolerance = 0.02)
sc <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "pinkert", "pinkert_species_countries.csv"))
support <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry", "country_realm_support.csv"))
support <- support[support$supported == "TRUE", ]

# Country-realm part code of each cell's representative point (as in the geometry section)
country_r <- rast(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry", "country_0p05.tif"))
part_r <- country_r * 100 + realm_r
cells[, part := extract(part_r, as.matrix(cells[, .(lon, lat)]))[, 1]]
cat("cells with a country-realm code:", sum(!is.na(cells$part)), "of", nrow(cells), "\n")

# --- Apply the rule to the cells of each unit ---
cells_by_unit <- split(cells, by = "pool_key")
n_done <- 0L
res <- vector("list", length(cells_by_unit))
names(res) <- names(cells_by_unit)
for (pk in names(res)) {
  ce <- copy(cells_by_unit[[pk]])
  n_done <- n_done + 1L
  if (n_done %% 250L == 0L) cat("native-region units:", n_done, "of", length(res),
                                format(Sys.time(), "%H:%M:%S"), "\n")

  # Distance of each cell to the listed area, and whether the checklist is reliable
  # (without a list the status is "no_list")
  iso <- unique(sc$iso3[sc$representative_key %in% pk])
  ce[, `:=`(d_listed_km = NA_real_, pinkert_status = "no_list")]
  if (length(iso)) {
    sup <- support[support$iso3 %in% iso, ]
    pv <- parts[parts$iso3 %in% iso &
                  paste(parts$iso3, parts$realm) %in% paste(sup$iso3, sup$realm), ]
    if (nrow(pv)) {
      # Cells whose 5-km country-realm code is a listed supported part are inside the listed
      # area (d = 0); geodesic distances to the (simplified) part polygons are computed only
      # for the remaining cells.
      inside <- ce$part %in% as.integer(sup$part)
      ce$d_listed_km <- 0
      if (any(!inside)) {
        pp <- vect(as.matrix(ce[!inside, .(lon, lat)]), crs = "EPSG:4326")
        dm <- distance(pp, pv) / 1000
        ce$d_listed_km[!inside] <- apply(dm, 1, min)
      }
      sup_realms <- unique(sup$realm)
      ce$realm_supported <- ce$realm %in% sup_realms

      # The checklist is used when enough cells are close to the listed area
      coverage <- mean(ce$d_listed_km <= parameters$pinkert_reliability_buffer_km)
      ce$pinkert_coverage <- coverage
      ce$pinkert_status <-
        if (coverage >= parameters$pinkert_reliability_min_coverage) "used" else "conflict"
    }
  }

  # --- Cells to remove ---
  if (ce$pinkert_status[1] == "used") {
    # Reliable checklist: remove cells far from the listed area
    ce$remove_native_main <-
      (ce$d_listed_km > parameters$pinkert_remove_other_realm_km & !ce$realm_supported) |
      ce$d_listed_km > parameters$pinkert_remove_any_realm_km
    ce$remove_native_strict <- ce$d_listed_km > parameters$pinkert_remove_strict_km
    ce$native_rule <- "pinkert"
  } else {
    # Data-driven fallback on realms: realms with enough cells or datasets are native
    rs <- ce[, .(cells = .N, datasets = sum(n_datasets)), by = realm]
    rs[, share := cells / sum(cells)]
    sup_r <- rs$realm[rs$share >= parameters$fallback_realm_min_cell_share |
                        rs$datasets >= parameters$fallback_realm_min_datasets]
    sup_r <- sup_r[!is.na(sup_r)]
    ce$realm_supported <- ce$realm %in% sup_r | is.na(ce$realm)

    # Cells in other realms are removed when far from the cells of the native realms
    ce$remove_native_main <- FALSE
    if (any(!ce$realm_supported) && any(ce$realm_supported)) {
      a <- vect(as.matrix(ce[realm_supported == FALSE, .(lon, lat)]), crs = "EPSG:4326")
      b <- vect(as.matrix(ce[realm_supported == TRUE, .(lon, lat)]), crs = "EPSG:4326")
      dd <- apply(distance(a, b) / 1000, 1, min)
      ce$remove_native_main[!ce$realm_supported] <- dd > parameters$fallback_remove_km
    }
    ce$remove_native_strict <- ce$remove_native_main
    ce$native_rule <- paste0("fallback_", ce$pinkert_status[1])

    # Wrong-continent override when the list is unreliable (see the section introduction)
    if (ce$pinkert_status[1] == "conflict") {
      far <- ce$d_listed_km > parameters$pinkert_remove_any_realm_km &
        !(ce$realm %in% sup_realms)
      if (any(far) && mean(far) < 0.5) {
        ce$remove_native_main <- ce$remove_native_main | far
        ce$remove_native_strict <- ce$remove_native_strict | far
        ce$native_rule <- "fallback_conflict+wrong_continent"
      }
    }
  }
  res[[pk]] <- ce
}

# --- Summary per unit ---
cells_native <- rbindlist(res, fill = TRUE)
summ <- cells_native[, .(cells = .N,
                         pinkert_status = pinkert_status[1],
                         native_rule = native_rule[1],
                         pinkert_coverage = pinkert_coverage[1],
                         cells_removed_main = sum(remove_native_main),
                         cells_removed_strict = sum(remove_native_strict)),
                     by = pool_key]
summ[, species := slim$rep_species[match(pool_key, slim$pool_key)]]
write_table(summ, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "native", "species_native_summary.csv"))
print(summ[, .N, by = native_rule])
cat("cells removed (main):", sum(cells_native$remove_native_main), "of", nrow(cells_native),
    "; species affected:", sum(summ$cells_removed_main > 0), "\n")

# --- Flags on the records ---
# Records outside the cell table (not in base_main) are not removed
slim <- merge(slim, cells_native[, .(pool_key, cell25, remove_native_main,
                                     remove_native_strict)],
              by = c("pool_key", "cell25"), all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
slim[is.na(remove_native_main),
     `:=`(remove_native_main = FALSE, remove_native_strict = FALSE)]
saveRDS(slim, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_base.rds"), compress = "gzip")
```

```{r clear_flag_native_regions, include=FALSE}
invisible(gc())
```
