# Introductions and outliers

Nine documented introductions and four species-concept errors (e.g. *Celastrina argiolus* records in the Americas) are removed by cited geographic rules. Outlying groups of localities are then found by single-linkage clustering of one locality per 25-km cell: a group of at most 10% of localities (or two) is an outlier if its gap to the rest exceeds 250 km and half the diameter of the remaining localities (main; groups corroborated by independent sources within 100 km are kept) or 200 km and a quarter of the diameter (strict_plus; all groups removed). Removal never leaves a species with fewer than five unique localities. The step defines the three datasets and writes the final record table and the record counts reported in the paper.

*Inputs:* records_base.rds; s01/species_traits.csv; occurrence_cleaning/{introduced_populations,taxonomic_range_exclusions}.csv  
*Outputs:* records_final.rds, outlier_groups.csv, dataset_counts.csv

```{r read_base_records}
# Records with the base flags, native-region removals and cell ids
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_base.rds"))
```

## Introduced populations and species-concept exclusions

Each curated rule flags the records of one species outside listed realms, in listed countries or in a bounding box.

```{r apply_curated_rules}
# Representative key of each GBIF key
traits <- read_chr(file.path(dir_s01, "species_traits.csv"))
rep_of <- setNames(traits$representative_key, traits$gbif_key)

# Flag the records that each rule of a curated table selects, in the new logical column
# `flag` of x (modified by reference). The rule types are realm_not_in (records outside the
# listed realms), countries (records in the listed countries) and bbox (records inside a
# box whose limits are listed as longitude minimum and maximum, then latitude minimum and
# maximum).
apply_rules <- function(tab, flag) {
  x[, (flag) := FALSE]
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(tab))) {
    # Records of the rule's unit, and the values of the rule
    pk <- unname(rep_of[tab$gbif_key[i]])
    vals <- strsplit(tab$rule_value[i], ";")[[1]]
    sel <- x$pool_key == pk & !is.na(x$pool_key)

    # Records of the unit that the rule selects
    hit <- switch(tab$rule_type[i],
      realm_not_in = sel & !is.na(x$realm) & !x$realm %in% vals,
      countries = sel & !is.na(x$iso3) & x$iso3 %in% vals,
      bbox = {
        b <- as.numeric(vals)
        sel & x$decimalLongitude >= b[1] & x$decimalLongitude <= b[2] &
          x$decimalLatitude >= b[3] & x$decimalLatitude <= b[4]
      },
      stop("unknown rule type ", tab$rule_type[i]))
    x[hit, (flag) := TRUE]
    cat(sprintf("%-14s %-24s %-13s records flagged: %d\n", flag, tab$species[i],
                tab$rule_type[i], sum(hit)))
  }
}

# Introduced populations and species-concept exclusions
apply_rules(read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "occurrence_cleaning",
                               "introduced_populations.csv")),
            "flag_introduced")
apply_rules(read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "occurrence_cleaning",
                               "taxonomic_range_exclusions.csv")),
            "flag_taxonomic_exclusion")

# Species-concept exclusions are removed from the base sets of main and inclusive
x[flag_taxonomic_exclusion == TRUE, `:=`(base_main = FALSE, base_inclusive = FALSE)]
```

## Outliers

Outlying groups of localities are found by the proportional gap rule below, applied repeatedly so that outliers cannot mask each other. In `main`, a group is kept if independent sources report it within 100 km of each other. In both datasets, removal never leaves a species with fewer than five unique localities.

```{r define_outlier_functions}
#' Great-circle distance matrix (km) between points given in degrees.
#' @param lon,lat Numeric vectors (degrees).
#' @return Symmetric numeric matrix in kilometres.
gc_distance_matrix <- function(lon, lat) {
  stopifnot(length(lon) == length(lat))
  r <- pi / 180

  # Unit vectors of the points; their dot product is the cosine of the central angle
  x <- cos(lat * r) * cos(lon * r)
  y <- cos(lat * r) * sin(lon * r)
  z <- sin(lat * r)
  dot <- outer(x, x) + outer(y, y) + outer(z, z)

  # Rounding can push the dot product beyond -1 and 1; the replacement keeps matrix dims
  dot[dot > 1] <- 1
  dot[dot < -1] <- -1

  # Distance with the mean Earth radius
  6371.0088 * acos(dot)
}

#' Flag outlier groups among thinned localities with the proportional gap rule.
#'
#' Localities are clustered by single linkage on great-circle distance. Every
#' subtree G of the dendrogram is a candidate. In single linkage the minimum
#' distance between G and all other localities equals the height at which G
#' joins its parent, so gap(G) is read directly from the tree. G is an outlier
#' group if (1) gap > f x diameter of the remaining localities (computed
#' without G, so an outlier cannot inflate its own yardstick), (2) gap >
#' floor_km, and (3) |G| <= max(2, minority_share x n) while at least three
#' localities remain. Groups are removed one at a time, the most extreme first
#' (largest gap / rest diameter), and the rule is re-applied to the remaining
#' localities (outliers can mask each other); the total flagged never exceeds
#' the size limit. Taking one group per pass matters in small samples: a pass
#' that finds more groups than the limit allows would otherwise flag nothing.
#' @param lon,lat Coordinates of unique thinned localities (degrees).
#' @param f Proportion of the remaining diameter that the gap must exceed.
#' @param floor_km Absolute minimum gap in km.
#' @param minority_share Maximum group size as a share of localities.
#' @return Data frame with one row per locality: `outlier` (logical),
#'   `group` (integer id of the flagged group, NA otherwise), `gap_km`,
#'   `rest_diameter_km` (for flagged groups).
flag_outlier_groups <- function(lon, lat, f = 0.5, floor_km = 250, minority_share = 0.1) {
  # Outliers can mask each other (a second distant point inflates the "rest"
  # diameter), so the rule is applied repeatedly to the not-yet-flagged
  # localities until no new group is found. The minority limit stays relative
  # to the original number of localities.
  n <- length(lon)
  out <- data.frame(outlier = rep(FALSE, n), group = NA_integer_,
                    gap_km = NA_real_, rest_diameter_km = NA_real_)
  max_size <- max(2L, floor(minority_share * n))
  gid <- 0L
  repeat {
    keep <- which(!out$outlier)
    if (length(keep) < 3L) break

    # Localities that may still be flagged: the size limit minus those flagged already, and
    # at least three localities must remain
    room <- min(max_size - sum(out$outlier), length(keep) - 3L)
    if (room < 1L) break
    r <- flag_outlier_groups_once(lon[keep], lat[keep], f, floor_km, room)
    if (!any(r$outlier)) break

    # Take only the most extreme flagged group in this pass
    gs <- unique(r$group[r$outlier])
    strength <- vapply(gs, function(g) {
      i <- which(r$group == g)[1]
      r$gap_km[i] / max(r$rest_diameter_km[i], 1e-9)
    }, 0)
    g_best <- gs[which.max(strength)]
    sel <- which(r$group == g_best)
    hit <- keep[sel]
    gid <- gid + 1L
    out$outlier[hit] <- TRUE
    out$group[hit] <- gid
    out$gap_km[hit] <- r$gap_km[sel]
    out$rest_diameter_km[hit] <- r$rest_diameter_km[sel]
  }
  out
}

#' One pass of the proportional gap rule (used by flag_outlier_groups()).
#' @param max_size Largest group size that may be flagged.
#' @return Data frame as returned by flag_outlier_groups().
flag_outlier_groups_once <- function(lon, lat, f, floor_km, max_size) {
  n <- length(lon)
  out <- data.frame(outlier = rep(FALSE, n), group = NA_integer_,
                    gap_km = NA_real_, rest_diameter_km = NA_real_)
  if (n < 3L) return(out)

  # --- Single-linkage tree ---
  D <- gc_distance_matrix(lon, lat)
  hc <- stats::hclust(stats::as.dist(D), method = "single")

  # Members of each merge node (negative = singleton)
  members <- vector("list", n - 1L)
  get_members <- function(k) if (k < 0) -k else members[[k]]
  for (k in seq_len(n - 1L)) members[[k]] <- c(get_members(hc$merge[k, 1]),
                                               get_members(hc$merge[k, 2]))

  # Height at which each node (singleton or merge) joins its parent
  parent_height_single <- numeric(n)
  parent_height_node <- rep(NA_real_, n - 1L)
  for (k in seq_len(n - 1L)) for (s in 1:2) {
    child <- hc$merge[k, s]
    if (child < 0) parent_height_single[-child] <- hc$height[k] else
      parent_height_node[child] <- hc$height[k]
  }

  # Global diameter pair, reused when G does not contain either end
  ij <- which(D == max(D), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
  diameter_without <- function(g) {
    if (!any(ij %in% g)) return(D[ij[1], ij[2]])
    keep <- setdiff(seq_len(n), g)
    if (length(keep) < 2L) return(0)
    max(D[keep, keep])
  }

  # --- Candidate groups ---
  # Every singleton, and every merge node of at most max_size members; the loop over the
  # merges stops before the root (the last merge), which has no parent
  cand <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n)) cand[[length(cand) + 1L]] <- list(g = i,
                                                          gap = parent_height_single[i])
  for (k in seq_len(n - 2L)) {
    if (length(members[[k]]) <= max_size)
      cand[[length(cand) + 1L]] <- list(g = members[[k]], gap = parent_height_node[k])
  }

  # --- Flag the groups with a large gap ---
  flagged <- list()
  for (cnd in cand) {
    if (length(cnd$g) > max_size || is.na(cnd$gap) || cnd$gap <= floor_km) next
    rest_d <- diameter_without(cnd$g)
    if (cnd$gap > f * rest_d) flagged[[length(flagged) + 1L]] <-
      list(g = cnd$g, gap = cnd$gap, rest = rest_d)
  }
  if (!length(flagged)) return(out)

  # Keep maximal groups only
  sizes <- vapply(flagged, function(z) length(z$g), 1L)
  flagged <- flagged[order(-sizes)]
  gid <- 0L
  for (z in flagged) {
    if (any(out$outlier[z$g])) next
    gid <- gid + 1L
    out$outlier[z$g] <- TRUE
    out$group[z$g] <- gid
    out$gap_km[z$g] <- z$gap
    out$rest_diameter_km[z$g] <- z$rest
  }
  out
}

#' Decide whether outlier groups are corroborated by independent sources.
#' @param group Integer outlier-group id per record (NA = not an outlier).
#' @param dataset,year,recorder Record-level metadata (same length as group).
#' @param min_datasets Distinct datasetKeys needed.
#' @param min_years,min_recorders Alternative: one dataset with this many
#'   distinct years AND recorders.
#' @param lon,lat Record coordinates (degrees).
#' @param radius_km Records support each other only within this distance.
#' @return Logical per record: TRUE if the record's group is corroborated.
corroborated_groups <- function(group, dataset, year, recorder, min_datasets = 2L,
                                min_years = 2L, min_recorders = 2L,
                                lon, lat, radius_km = 100) {
  # Corroboration is local: independent sources must report the same place. Records of a group
  # are sub-clustered (single linkage, radius_km); the group is corroborated if any
  # sub-cluster meets the rule.
  ok_rule <- function(i) {
    nd <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(dataset[i])))
    ny <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(year[i])))
    rr <- recorder[i]
    nr <- length(unique(stats::na.omit(rr[!is.na(rr) & nzchar(rr)])))
    nd >= min_datasets || (ny >= min_years && nr >= min_recorders)
  }
  res <- rep(FALSE, length(group))
  for (g in unique(stats::na.omit(group))) {
    i <- which(group == g)
    if (length(i) < 2L) {
      res[i] <- ok_rule(i)
      next
    }
    u <- unique(data.frame(lon = lon[i], lat = lat[i]))
    sub <- if (nrow(u) > 1L)
      stats::cutree(stats::hclust(stats::as.dist(gc_distance_matrix(u$lon, u$lat)),
                                  method = "single"), h = radius_km) else 1L
    key <- sub[match(paste(lon[i], lat[i]), paste(u$lon, u$lat))]
    res[i] <- any(vapply(unique(key), function(s) ok_rule(i[key == s]), TRUE))
  }
  res
}

#' Cap outlier removal so that a unit keeps the range minimum
#'
#' If removing the flagged records would leave fewer than `min_localities`
#' unique localities in a unit that had at least that many, flagged groups are
#' restored in reverse peeling order (highest group id = least extreme first)
#' until the minimum is met.
#' @param group Outlier-group id per record (NA = not an outlier); ids follow
#'   the peeling order of flag_outlier_groups().
#' @param remove Logical per record: currently scheduled for removal.
#' @param lon,lat Record coordinates (unique localities are distinct pairs).
#' @param min_localities Minimum number of unique localities to keep.
#' @return List: `remove` (updated logical) and `restored` (restored group ids).
cap_outlier_removal <- function(group, remove, lon, lat, min_localities = 5L) {
  # Number of unique localities among the selected records
  uloc <- function(sel) nrow(unique(data.frame(lon = lon[sel], lat = lat[sel])))
  restored <- integer(0)
  if (any(remove) && uloc(rep(TRUE, length(remove))) >= min_localities) {
    for (g in sort(unique(group[remove]), decreasing = TRUE)) {
      if (uloc(!remove) >= min_localities) break
      remove[group %in% g] <- FALSE
      restored <- c(restored, g)
    }
  }
  list(remove = remove, restored = restored)
}
```

```{r flag_outliers}
# --- Outlier groups of one unit ---
# Coarser grid for units that occupy many 25-km cells
grid50 <- global_thinning_grid(parameters$outlier_cell_km_large)

# Flag the outlier groups among the records `rec` of one unit (a data.table with the
# column cell25) with the gap rule `f` and `floor_km`. `corroborate` sets whether
# corroborated groups are kept (main) or not (strict_plus). Returns a list: `remove`
# (logical per record), `restored` (groups restored to keep the minimum of localities),
# `rec` (the records with their group and corroboration) and `cells` (the localities with
# their group and gap).
detect <- function(rec, f, floor_km, corroborate) {
  # One locality per cell; cells of 50 km if the unit occupies many 25-km cells
  cl <- rec[, .(lon = decimalLongitude[1], lat = decimalLatitude[1]), by = cell25]
  cell_col <- "cell25"
  if (nrow(cl) > parameters$outlier_large_cells) {
    pts <- project(vect(as.matrix(rec[, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]),
                        crs = "EPSG:4326"),
                   crs(grid50))
    rec[, cell50 := cellFromXY(grid50, crds(pts))]
    cl <- rec[, .(lon = decimalLongitude[1], lat = decimalLatitude[1]), by = cell50]
    cell_col <- "cell50"
  }

  # Outlier groups among the localities, carried back to the records of their cells
  r <- flag_outlier_groups(cl$lon, cl$lat, f = f, floor_km = floor_km,
                           minority_share = parameters$outlier_minority_share)
  cl$group <- r$group
  cl$gap_km <- r$gap_km
  cl$rest_diameter_km <- r$rest_diameter_km
  rec$group <- cl$group[match(rec[[cell_col]], cl[[cell_col]])]

  # Corroboration by independent sources (only when `corroborate` is TRUE)
  rec$corroborated <- if (corroborate && any(!is.na(rec$group))) corroborated_groups(
    rec$group, rec$datasetKey, rec$year, rec$recordedBy,
    min_datasets = parameters$corroboration_min_datasets,
    min_years = parameters$corroboration_single_dataset_years,
    min_recorders = parameters$corroboration_single_dataset_recorders,
    lon = rec$decimalLongitude, lat = rec$decimalLatitude,
    radius_km = parameters$corroboration_radius_km) else FALSE

  # Removal must not take a unit below the range minimum of unique localities
  remove <- !is.na(rec$group) & !rec$corroborated
  cap <- cap_outlier_removal(rec$group, remove, rec$decimalLongitude, rec$decimalLatitude,
                             min_localities = parameters$min_unique_localities)
  list(remove = cap$remove, restored = cap$restored, rec = rec, cells = cl)
}

# --- Detect the outliers of every unit ---
x[, `:=`(outlier_main = FALSE, outlier_strict = FALSE)]
x[, row_id := .I]

# Records entering the outlier rule: base_main records that are not removed by the
# native-region filter or as introduced, split by unit
pre_main <- x[base_main & !remove_native_main & !flag_introduced]
pre_strict <- x[base_main & !remove_native_strict & !flag_introduced]
groups_out <- list()
main_by_unit <- split(pre_main, by = "pool_key")
strict_by_unit <- split(pre_strict, by = "pool_key")
units <- sort(names(main_by_unit))
for (j in seq_along(units)) {
  pk <- units[j]
  for (variant in c("main", "strict")) {
    rec <- if (variant == "main") main_by_unit[[pk]] else strict_by_unit[[pk]]
    if (is.null(rec)) next
    rec <- copy(rec)
    if (nrow(rec) < 3L) next

    # main: its gap rule with corroboration; strict: its gap rule without corroboration
    r <- if (variant == "main") detect(rec, parameters$outlier_f_main,
                                       parameters$outlier_floor_main_km, TRUE) else
      detect(rec, parameters$outlier_f_strict, parameters$outlier_floor_strict_km, FALSE)

    # Mark the records to remove
    if (any(r$remove)) set(x, i = r$rec$row_id[r$remove], j = paste0("outlier_", variant),
                           value = TRUE)

    # One row per outlier group: size, sources, centroid, gap and number of cells
    g <- r$rec[!is.na(group), .(records = .N, datasets = uniqueN(datasetKey),
                                years = uniqueN(year), recorders = uniqueN(recordedBy),
                                corroborated = corroborated[1],
                                lon = mean(decimalLongitude), lat = mean(decimalLatitude)),
               by = group]
    if (nrow(g)) {
      cg <- r$cells[!is.na(group), .(gap_km = gap_km[1],
                                     rest_diameter_km = rest_diameter_km[1],
                                     cells = .N),
                    by = group]
      g <- merge(g, cg, by = "group")
      g[, kept_min_localities := group %in% r$restored]

      # A group is removed unless it is corroborated (main only) or restored to keep the
      # minimum of localities
      g[, `:=`(pool_key = pk, variant = variant,
               removed = (!corroborated | variant == "strict") & !kept_min_localities)]
      groups_out[[length(groups_out) + 1L]] <- g
    }
  }
  if (j %% 250 == 0) cat("outliers:", j, "of", length(units), "\n")
}

# --- Outlier groups table ---
og <- rbindlist(groups_out, fill = TRUE)
og[, species := x$rep_species[match(pool_key, x$pool_key)]]
write_table(og, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "outlier_groups.csv"))

# --- The three datasets and the record counts ---
x[, in_inclusive := base_inclusive]
x[, in_main := base_main & !remove_native_main & !flag_introduced & !outlier_main]
x[, in_strict_plus := base_main & !remove_native_strict & !flag_introduced &
      !outlier_strict]
counts <- data.frame(
  stage = c("all_records_with_coordinates", "base_inclusive", "base_main",
            "native_removed_main", "introduced_removed", "outlier_removed_main",
            "final_main", "final_strict_plus", "final_inclusive"),
  records = c(nrow(x), sum(x$base_inclusive), sum(x$base_main),
              sum(x$base_main & x$remove_native_main),
              sum(x$base_main & !x$remove_native_main & x$flag_introduced),
              sum(x$outlier_main), sum(x$in_main), sum(x$in_strict_plus),
              sum(x$in_inclusive)))
write_table(counts, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "dataset_counts.csv"))
print(counts, row.names = FALSE)
cat("outlier groups (main):", og[variant == "main", .N],
    "; removed:", og[variant == "main" & removed == TRUE, .N],
    "; corroborated kept:", og[variant == "main" & corroborated == TRUE, .N],
    "; kept to stay >= minimum localities:",
    og[variant == "main" & kept_min_localities == TRUE, .N],
    "(strict:", og[variant == "strict" & kept_min_localities == TRUE, .N], ")\n")

# --- Save the final records ---
x[, row_id := NULL]
saveRDS(x, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_final.rds"), compress = "gzip")
```

# Range measurement

Species with at least five unique localities are thinned (50-km Equal Earth cells for species spanning more than five cells, then 10-km great-circle distance, with MCP vertices restored) and measured: latitudinal extent, circular longitudinal extent, MCP area in a species-specific cylindrical equal-area projection and the stability of each measure (mean of 1,000 random 80% subsamples divided by the full estimate; Gupta et al. 2020). Seeds are derived from each species' GBIF key, so results do not depend on the other species or on the number of parallel workers (`n_workers`). Per-species checkpoints in `ranges/checkpoints/` let an interrupted run resume.

*Inputs:* records_final.rds  
*Outputs:* ranges/range_main.csv, ranges/thinning_audit.csv, ranges/range_inclusive.csv, ranges/range_strict_plus.csv

```{r prepare_range_workers}
out_dir <- file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "ranges")

# --- Unique localities per unit ---
# Unique localities of each dataset, for units with enough of them
localities <- local({
  x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_final.rds"))
  occ_list <- function(flag) {
    y <- x[get(flag) == TRUE, .(pool_key, decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]
    y <- unique(y)
    s <- split(as.data.frame(y[, .(decimalLongitude, decimalLatitude)]), y$pool_key)
    s[vapply(s, nrow, 1L) >= parameters$min_unique_localities]
  }
  list(main = occ_list("in_main"),
       inclusive = occ_list("in_inclusive"),
       strict = occ_list("in_strict_plus"))
})
invisible(gc())
main <- localities$main[order(names(localities$main))]
cat("eligible units: main", length(main), "; inclusive", length(localities$inclusive),
    "; strict_plus", length(localities$strict), "\n")

# --- Worker setup ---
# Each worker sources the range helpers and builds the coarse thinning grid once. Their md5
# sums enter the checkpoint fingerprints, so editing them invalidates the checkpoints.
helper_files <- here::here("code", "R", c("range_metrics.R", "projections.R", "thinning.R"))
code_hash <- unname(tools::md5sum(helper_files))
setup_worker <- function(helper_files, cell_km) {
  for (f in helper_files) source(f)
  assign("thin_grid", global_thinning_grid(cell_km), envir = globalenv())
  TRUE
}

# --- Checkpoints ---
# A unit's checkpointed result if its fingerprint matches; otherwise compute and save it.
# `ck` is the checkpoint file and `compute` a function that returns the result.
cached_result <- function(ck, fingerprint, compute) {
  old <- if (file.exists(ck)) tryCatch(readRDS(ck), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (identical(old$fingerprint, fingerprint)) return(old$result)
  out <- compute()

  # Write, then rename: no truncated checkpoints
  tmp <- paste0(ck, ".tmp")
  saveRDS(list(fingerprint = fingerprint, result = out), tmp)
  unlink(ck)
  file.rename(tmp, ck)
  out
}

# --- Functions run on the workers ---
# Thinning, full-range metrics and 80% rarefaction stability of unit i (run on a worker). The
# unit is element i of the list called `units_name` on the worker. Returns a list with the
# metrics, the thinning audit and the number of unique localities.
main_one <- function(i, ck_dir, thin_seed, range_seed, n_rep, cell_km, distance_km, code_hash,
                     units_name) {
  units <- get(units_name, envir = globalenv())
  pk <- names(units)[i]
  y <- units[[i]]

  # The pool key is added to the seeds (GBIF keys < 2^31 - seed base)
  k <- as.numeric(pk)
  if (is.na(k)) stop("non-numeric pool key ", pk)
  fingerprint <- rlang::hash(list(y$decimalLongitude, y$decimalLatitude,
                                  thin_seed, range_seed, n_rep,
                                  cell_km, distance_km, code_hash))
  cached_result(file.path(ck_dir, paste0(pk, ".rds")), fingerprint, function() {
    # Thinned localities and the audit of the thinning
    th <- thin_species(y, thin_grid, cell_km = cell_km, distance_km = distance_km,
                       seed = thin_seed + k)
    au <- cbind(pool_key = pk, attr(th, "thinning_audit"))

    # Range metrics and stability of the thinned points
    rm_ <- range_metrics(stats::setNames(list(th), pk), n_rep = n_rep, seed = range_seed + k,
                         metric_function = projected_mcp_extent_area,
                         fixed_longitude_reference = TRUE, fixed_projection = TRUE)
    rm_$range_basis <- "thinned_points"
    if (nrow(th) < 5L) {
      # range_metrics() needs >= 5 points after the random thinning; the full-range
      # metrics do not depend on thinning, so they come from the unique localities exactly
      # as range_metrics() computes them.
      prj <- species_cea_crs(y$decimalLongitude)
      full <- projected_mcp_extent_area(
        project_species_cea(y, prj),
        longitude_reference_latitude = mean(range(y$decimalLatitude)),
        projection = prj,
        include_s2_audit = TRUE)
      rm_ <- data.frame(species = pk, t(full), occurrence_count = nrow(th),
                        asympt_prop_lat = NA, asympt_prop_lon = NA, asympt_prop_area = NA,
                        range_basis = "unique_localities", check.names = FALSE)
    }
    list(metrics = rm_, audit = au, unique_localities = nrow(y))
  })
}

# Full-range metrics of unit i without thinning (run on a worker). Returns a one-row data
# frame.
full_one <- function(i, ck_dir, code_hash) {
  units <- get("units_full", envir = globalenv())
  pk <- names(units)[i]
  y <- units[[i]]
  fingerprint <- rlang::hash(list(y$decimalLongitude, y$decimalLatitude, code_hash))
  cached_result(file.path(ck_dir, paste0(pk, ".rds")), fingerprint, function() {
    m <- projected_mcp_extent_area(y, include_s2_audit = FALSE)
    data.frame(pool_key = pk,
               t(m[c("latitudinal_extent", "longitudinal_extent", "range_area",
                     "midpoint_latitude", "midpoint_longitude")]),
               unique_localities = nrow(y))
  })
}

# --- Functions run on the main process ---
# Checkpoint folder of one run, without files of units that no longer exist
checkpoint_dir <- function(name, units) {
  d <- file.path(out_dir, "checkpoints", name)
  dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  unlink(setdiff(list.files(d, full.names = TRUE),
                 file.path(d, paste0(names(units), ".rds"))))
  d
}

# Thin, measure and rarefy units on the workers; results follow the order of `ord`
# (largest units first). `units_name` is the name under which the workers receive the
# units and `ck_name` the name of the checkpoint folder.
rarefy_units <- function(units, units_name, ck_name) {
  assign(units_name, units, envir = globalenv())
  parallel::clusterExport(cl, units_name)

  # Large units first so that workers stay balanced
  ord <- order(-vapply(units, nrow, 1L))
  parallel::clusterApplyLB(cl, ord, main_one, ck_dir = checkpoint_dir(ck_name, units),
                           thin_seed = parameters$thin_seed,
                           range_seed = parameters$rarefaction_seed,
                           n_rep = parameters$rarefaction_reps,
                           cell_km = parameters$thin_cell_km,
                           distance_km = parameters$thin_distance_km,
                           code_hash = code_hash,
                           units_name = units_name)
}

# --- Start the workers ---
cl <- parallel::makeCluster(n_workers)
invisible(parallel::clusterCall(cl, setup_worker, helper_files, parameters$thin_cell_km))
parallel::clusterExport(cl, "cached_result")
```

```{r measure_main_ranges}
# --- Measure the main dataset ---
t0 <- Sys.time()
res <- rarefy_units(main, "units_main", "main")
cat("main done in", format(Sys.time() - t0), "\n")

# --- Collect and save the results ---
range_main <- rbindlist(
  lapply(res, function(r) cbind(r$metrics, unique_localities = r$unique_localities)),
  fill = TRUE)
setnames(range_main, "species", "pool_key")
audit <- rbindlist(lapply(res, `[[`, "audit"), fill = TRUE)
write_table(range_main, file.path(out_dir, "range_main.csv"))
write_table(audit, file.path(out_dir, "thinning_audit.csv"))
```

## Inclusive and strict_plus

The full-range metrics of both datasets are computed without thinning; `strict_plus` also gets the stability measures, with the thinning, rarefaction and seeds of `main`.

```{r measure_other_ranges}
# Full-range metrics of inclusive and strict_plus, computed without thinning
for (v in c("inclusive", "strict_plus")) {
  units <- if (v == "inclusive") localities$inclusive else localities$strict
  units <- units[order(names(units))]
  units_full <- units
  parallel::clusterExport(cl, "units_full")
  r <- rbindlist(parallel::clusterApplyLB(cl, seq_along(units), full_one,
                                          ck_dir = checkpoint_dir(v, units),
                                          code_hash = code_hash))

  # strict_plus also gets the stability measures
  if (v == "strict_plus") {
    # Same thinning, rarefaction and per-unit seeds as main, so units whose strict and main
    # localities are identical get identical stability values.
    rs <- rarefy_units(units, "units_strict", "strict_plus_rarefaction")
    st <- rbindlist(lapply(rs, `[[`, "metrics"), fill = TRUE)
    st <- st[, .(pool_key = species, asympt_prop_lat, asympt_prop_lon, asympt_prop_area)]
    r <- merge(r, st, by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
  }
  write_table(r, file.path(out_dir, paste0("range_", v, ".csv")))
  cat(v, "done\n")
}

# Stop the workers
parallel::stopCluster(cl)
```

# Range table

One row per species of the trait table combines record counts per cleaning stage, the range measures of the three datasets, the native-region rule and documented introductions; internal consistency checks stop the notebook if they fail. The cleaning parameters are saved beside the table.

*Inputs:* records_final.rds; ranges/*.csv; native/species_native_summary.csv; geometry/pinkert_species_realms.csv; s01/species_traits.csv; taxonomy/{genus_subfamily,riodinid_genera}.csv; occurrence_cleaning/introduced_populations.csv  
*Outputs:* range_metrics.csv, parameters.csv

```{r range_table_species}
# --- Units of the range table ---
# One row per representative species of the trait table, except riodinids
traits <- as.data.table(read_chr(file.path(dir_s01, "species_traits.csv")))

U <- traits[universe_status == "gbif_accepted" & gbif_key == representative_key &
              !genus %in% rio,
            .(species, gbif_key, genus)]

# Subfamily from the genus table
gs <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "taxonomy", "genus_subfamily.csv"))
U[, subfamily := gs$combined_subfamily[match(genus, gs$genus_unique)]]

# Each species starts as its own pool, with no other species pooled with it
U[, pool_key := gbif_key]
U[, pooled_with := ""]
```

## Record counts and range measures per unit

```{r range_table_columns}
# --- Record counts per unit ---
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_final.rds"))
cnt <- x[!is.na(pool_key), .(
  n_records_assigned = .N,
  n_base_main = sum(base_main),
  n_removed_native_main = sum(base_main & remove_native_main),
  n_removed_introduced = sum(base_main & !remove_native_main & flag_introduced),
  n_removed_outlier_main = sum(outlier_main),
  n_main = sum(in_main),
  n_inclusive = sum(in_inclusive),

  n_living_specimen_excluded = sum(basisOfRecord == "LIVING_SPECIMEN")),
  by = pool_key]

# --- Antimeridian crossing ---
# TRUE if the occupied longitudes wrap across -180/180 degrees: the shortest circular occupied
# arc is narrower than the ordinary minimum-to-maximum interval.
range_crosses_antimeridian <- function(longitude) {
  longitude <- longitude[is.finite(longitude)]
  if (length(longitude) < 2L) return(FALSE)
  circular_span <- unname(circular_longitude_extent(longitude,
                                                    reference_latitude = 0)["angular_span"])
  circular_span + 1e-10 < diff(range(longitude))
}
anti <- x[in_main == TRUE,
          .(crosses_antimeridian = range_crosses_antimeridian(unique(decimalLongitude))),
          by = pool_key]
rm(x)
invisible(gc())

# --- Range tables of the datasets ---
rg <- file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "ranges")
main <- fread(file.path(rg, "range_main.csv"), colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
audit <- fread(file.path(rg, "thinning_audit.csv"),
               colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
inc <- fread(file.path(rg, "range_inclusive.csv"), colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
strict <- fread(file.path(rg, "range_strict_plus.csv"),
                colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))

# --- Native-region summary, realms and introductions ---
nat <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "native", "species_native_summary.csv"),
             colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
sr <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "geometry", "pinkert_species_realms.csv"),
            colClasses = "character")
intro <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "occurrence_cleaning",
                            "introduced_populations.csv"))

# --- Combine the tables ---
# Record counts, then the main range measures and the thinning audit
out <- merge(U, cnt, by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
out <- merge(out, main, by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
out <- merge(out,
             audit[, .(pool_key, n_thinned = after_distance,
                       coarse_cell_thinning = cell_applied)],
             by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)

# Range measures of inclusive and strict_plus, with the dataset as column suffix
for (v in c("inclusive", "strict_plus")) {
  r <- if (v == "inclusive") inc else strict

  # Stability columns exist for strict_plus only
  cols <- intersect(c("pool_key", "latitudinal_extent", "longitudinal_extent", "range_area",
                      "unique_localities", "asympt_prop_lat", "asympt_prop_lon",
                      "asympt_prop_area"), names(r))
  r <- r[, ..cols]
  setnames(r, -1, paste0(names(r)[-1], "_", v))
  out <- merge(out, r, by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
}

# Native-region rule, antimeridian crossing, supported realms and introduced regions
out <- merge(out, nat[, .(pool_key, native_rule, pinkert_status, pinkert_coverage,
                          cells_removed_native_main = cells_removed_main,
                          cells_removed_native_strict = cells_removed_strict)],
             by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
out <- merge(out, anti, by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE)
out[, pinkert_supported_realms :=
      sr$supported_realms[match(gbif_key, sr$representative_key)]]
out[, introduced_regions := intro$introduced_range_note[match(gbif_key, intro$gbif_key)]]

# Low-data species, and species with a main range
out[, low_data := !is.na(unique_localities) &
      unique_localities < parameters$low_data_localities]
out[, has_range := is.finite(range_area) & range_area > 0]

# --- Column order and save ---
setcolorder(out, c("species", "gbif_key", "genus", "subfamily", "pool_key", "pooled_with",
                   "latitudinal_extent", "longitudinal_extent", "range_area",
                   "asympt_prop_lat", "asympt_prop_lon", "asympt_prop_area",
                   "occurrence_count", "unique_localities", "low_data", "has_range"))
out <- out[order(species)]
write_table(out, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "range_metrics.csv"))

# --- Parameters table ---
# Numbers without scientific notation; several values of one parameter separated by ";"
parameter_values <- vapply(parameters, function(v)
  paste(if (is.numeric(v)) format(v, scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE) else v,
        collapse = ";"), "")
write_table(data.frame(parameter = names(parameters), value = parameter_values),
            file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "parameters.csv"))
```

## Consistency checks

```{r check_range_table}
# --- Checks ---
# Each check is a row with its name, whether it passed and a detail
chk <- list()
add <- function(check, passed, detail = "") chk[[length(chk) + 1L]] <<-
  data.frame(check, passed, detail)

add("one row per representative species", !anyDuplicated(out$gbif_key),
    paste(nrow(out), "rows"))
add("rarefaction proportions <= 1",
    all(out[, c(asympt_prop_lat, asympt_prop_lon, asympt_prop_area)] <= 1 + 1e-10,
        na.rm = TRUE))
add("range area positive where computed", all(out$range_area[is.finite(out$range_area)] > 0))
add("main records are a subset of inclusive records (counts)",
    all(out$n_main <= out$n_inclusive, na.rm = TRUE))
add("main MCP area <= inclusive MCP area (subset hull)",
    all(out$range_area <= out$range_area_inclusive * (1 + 1e-6), na.rm = TRUE),
    paste(sum(out$range_area > out$range_area_inclusive * (1 + 1e-6), na.rm = TRUE),
          "violations"))
add("main latitudinal extent <= inclusive",
    all(out$latitudinal_extent <= out$latitudinal_extent_inclusive + 1e-6, na.rm = TRUE))
add("units with >= 5 localities keep >= 3 thinned points",
    all(out$n_thinned[out$unique_localities >= 5] >= 3, na.rm = TRUE))
add("species with a main range", TRUE, as.character(sum(out$has_range)))

# --- Report ---
# The notebook stops if a check failed
val <- do.call(rbind, chk)
print(val, row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nspecies rows:", nrow(out), "; with main range:", sum(out$has_range),
    "; low_data:", sum(out$low_data & out$has_range), "\n")
if (!all(val$passed)) stop("A range-table consistency check failed.", call. = FALSE)
```

```{r clear_build_range_table, include=FALSE}
invisible(gc())
```

# Expert-range validation

The ranges are compared with the independent expert range polygons of Hausharter et al. (2023) for mostly European species: the share of occupied cells inside the polygons (100-km buffer) and the correlation of log10 MCP area with expert range size.

*Inputs:* records_final.rds; range_metrics.csv; s01/species_traits.csv; gbif_backbone/ snapshot; taxonomy/riodinid_genera.csv; expert_ranges/{Butterfly_ranges/Butterfly_ranges.shp, Butterfly_data.csv, expert_species_correspondence.csv}  
*Outputs:* expert_validation_species.csv, expert_validation_summary.csv

```{r validate_expert_ranges}
# --- Occupied cells ---
# One row per occupied 25-km cell of the records in the inclusive or main base sets: the
# coordinates of its first record, whether it is in main or inclusive, and whether any of its
# records was removed by the native-region rule, as an outlier or as introduced
x <- readRDS(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "records_final.rds"))
cells <- x[!is.na(pool_key) & base_inclusive | (!is.na(pool_key) & base_main),
           .(lon = decimalLongitude[1], lat = decimalLatitude[1],
             main = any(in_main), inclusive = any(in_inclusive),
             removed_native = any(base_main & remove_native_main),
             removed_outlier = any(outlier_main),
             removed_introduced = any(base_main & flag_introduced)),
           by = .(pool_key, cell25)]
rm(x)
invisible(gc())

# --- Range table and lookups ---
fin <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "range_metrics.csv"),
             colClasses = c(gbif_key = "character", pool_key = "character"))
traits <- read_chr(file.path(dir_s01, "species_traits.csv"))
rep_of <- setNames(traits$representative_key, traits$gbif_key)
pool_of <- setNames(fin$pool_key, fin$gbif_key)

# --- Share of cells inside an expert range ---
# Share of the cell points `pts` (columns lon and lat) inside the expert polygon `poly`
# buffered by `buffer_m` metres; NA if there are no cells
inside_share <- function(pts, poly, buffer_m = 1e5) {
  if (!nrow(pts)) return(NA_real_)
  pb <- buffer(poly, buffer_m)
  v <- vect(as.matrix(pts[, .(lon, lat)]), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  mean(relate(v, aggregate(pb), "intersects")[, 1])
}

# --- Expert polygons and name correspondence ---
poly <- vect(file.path(dir_data_raw, "expert_ranges", "Butterfly_ranges",
                       "Butterfly_ranges.shp"))
poly <- project(poly, "EPSG:4326")
expert <- read.csv(file.path(dir_data_raw, "expert_ranges", "Butterfly_data.csv"))
corr <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "expert_ranges",
                           "expert_species_correspondence.csv"))
snapshot <- read_backbone_snapshot(dir_data_raw)

# GBIF key and pool key of each expert species: its GBIF name resolved in the snapshot (an
# accepted name or a synonym of one accepted species)
corr$gbif_key <- unname(rep_of[resolve_accepted_key(gsub("_", " ", corr$Hau2023_names_GBIF),
                                                    snapshot)])
corr$pool_key <- unname(pool_of[corr$gbif_key])

# --- Comparison per species ---
# For each expert species with a polygon: the share of its cells inside the buffered polygon
# (main, inclusive and removed cells), the number of removed cells and the expert range size
ev <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(corr)), function(i) {
  pk <- corr$pool_key[i]
  if (is.na(pk)) return(NULL)
  p <- poly[poly$species == corr$Hau2023_names[i], ]
  if (!nrow(p)) return(NULL)
  ce <- cells[pool_key == pk]
  data.table(species = corr$Hau2023_names_GBIF[i],
             pool_key = pk,
             share_inside_main = inside_share(ce[main == TRUE], p),
             share_inside_inclusive = inside_share(ce[inclusive == TRUE], p),
             share_inside_removed = inside_share(ce[removed_native | removed_outlier |
                                                      removed_introduced], p),
             n_removed_cells = ce[removed_native | removed_outlier | removed_introduced, .N],
             expert_area = expert$Range_size[match(gsub(" ", "_", corr$Hau2023_names[i]),
                                                   expert$Species)])
}))

# Range areas of the three datasets
ev <- merge(ev, fin[, .(pool_key, range_area, range_area_inclusive,
                        range_area_strict_plus)][!duplicated(pool_key)],
            by = "pool_key", all.x = TRUE)
write_table(ev, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "expert_validation_species.csv"))

# --- Summary ---
# Species with a positive main range area and expert range size, and a finite inclusive area
ok <- ev[is.finite(range_area) & is.finite(expert_area) & range_area > 0 & expert_area > 0 &
         is.finite(range_area_inclusive)]

# Number of species compared, median and mean shares inside, and correlations of range area
# with expert range size
es <- data.frame(
  species = nrow(ok),
  median_share_inside_main = median(ev$share_inside_main, na.rm = TRUE),
  median_share_inside_inclusive = median(ev$share_inside_inclusive, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_share_inside_main = mean(ev$share_inside_main, na.rm = TRUE),
  mean_share_inside_inclusive = mean(ev$share_inside_inclusive, na.rm = TRUE),
  share_inside_removed_cells = mean(ev$share_inside_removed, na.rm = TRUE),
  pearson_log_area_main = cor(log10(ok$range_area), log10(ok$expert_area)),
  pearson_log_area_inclusive = cor(log10(ok$range_area_inclusive), log10(ok$expert_area)),
  pearson_log_area_strict_plus = cor(log10(ok$range_area_strict_plus),
                                     log10(ok$expert_area), use = "complete.obs"),
  spearman_area_main = cor(ok$range_area, ok$expert_area, method = "spearman"),
  spearman_area_inclusive = cor(ok$range_area_inclusive, ok$expert_area, method = "spearman"))
write_table(es, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "expert_validation_summary.csv"))
print(t(es))
```

```{r clear_validate_expert_ranges, include=FALSE}
invisible(gc())
```

# Outlier-rule check

The share of outlier groups whose centroid lies inside the buffered expert polygons shows how often each rule removes plausibly genuine records: groups removed by the main rule, corroborated groups kept by it, and groups removed only by the strict rule (reported in Appendix S2).

*Inputs:* outlier_groups.csv; expert_validation_species.csv; expert_ranges/{Butterfly_ranges/Butterfly_ranges.shp, expert_species_correspondence.csv}  
*Output:* outlier_expert_check.csv

```{r check_outlier_rule}
# --- Outlier groups and expert polygons ---
og <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "outlier_groups.csv"),
            colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
ev <- fread(file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "expert_validation_species.csv"),
            colClasses = c(pool_key = "character"))
corr <- read_chr(file.path(dir_data_raw, "expert_ranges",
                           "expert_species_correspondence.csv"))
poly <- project(vect(file.path(dir_data_raw, "expert_ranges", "Butterfly_ranges",
                               "Butterfly_ranges.shp")),
                "EPSG:4326")

# Groups of the species with an expert comparison, with the expert name of each species
og <- og[pool_key %in% ev$pool_key]
og[, hau := corr$Hau2023_names[match(ev$species[match(pool_key, ev$pool_key)],
                                     corr$Hau2023_names_GBIF)]]
main <- og[variant == "main"]
strict <- og[variant == "strict"]

# --- Strict groups that the main rule also finds ---
# TRUE if a main group of the unit lies within 100 km of the centroid of the strict group
strict[, also_main := mapply(function(pk, lo, la) {
  m <- main[pool_key == pk]
  if (!nrow(m)) return(FALSE)
  any(geosphere::distHaversine(cbind(m$lon, m$lat), c(lo, la)) < 1e5)
}, pool_key, lon, lat)]

# --- Centroids inside the buffered expert polygon ---
# Logical per row of the group table g (NA if the species has no expert polygon); the polygon
# is buffered by 100 km
inside <- function(g) vapply(seq_len(nrow(g)), function(i) {
  p <- poly[poly$species == g$hau[i], ]
  if (!nrow(p)) return(NA)
  v <- vect(cbind(g$lon[i], g$lat[i]), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  relate(v, aggregate(buffer(p, 1e5)), "intersects")[1, 1]
}, TRUE)
main[, inside_expert := inside(main)]
strict_only <- strict[also_main == FALSE]
strict_only[, inside_expert := inside(strict_only)]

# --- Summary table ---
# Share of group centroids inside the expert range for the three sets of groups
res <- rbind(
  data.table(set = "main: removed (uncorroborated)", groups = main[removed == TRUE, .N],
             share_inside_expert = main[removed == TRUE, mean(inside_expert, na.rm = TRUE)]),
  data.table(set = "main: corroborated, kept", groups = main[removed == FALSE, .N],
             share_inside_expert = main[removed == FALSE, mean(inside_expert, na.rm = TRUE)]),
  data.table(set = "strict only (f 0.25, not flagged at f 0.5)", groups = nrow(strict_only),
             share_inside_expert = strict_only[, mean(inside_expert, na.rm = TRUE)]))
write_table(res, file.path(dir_data_intermediate, "outlier_expert_check.csv"))
print(res)
```
